strings.ui.free_h.title: Time together · %s
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_phar: Manami Iimura gathers the scattered tea bags into a box. Noticing Sakaguchi looking over, she smiles gently. “It’s not that I have to tidy everything. It’s just that if things are somewhere easy to see, the next person who comes in for a break won’t have to search for them.”

She slips her work pen into her pocket and lets out a soft breath. “I’m used to checking things over and over in the pharmacy. But here, it’s all right to take a little longer choosing a drink, isn’t it? At least no one will be affected if I pick the wrong tea.”

Sakaguchi mentions how some reminders can offend people. Iimura thinks for a moment. “We can try to speak gently, and apologize if necessary. But when something needs to be pointed out, we can’t pretend we haven’t noticed just to keep everyone happy.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_pha: Looking down at the distant streets, Iimura seems more relaxed than she does in the pharmacy. “People walk so quickly when you watch them from here. Sometimes I’d like to learn to slow down, too. Not to put off work—just to stop treating hurry as the right pace for everything.”

The wind makes her words a little hard to hear. Iimura smiles and raises her voice slightly. “Do I usually speak too quietly? This isn’t the pharmacy; just moving a little closer really won’t do here. Please tell me if you can’t hear me.”

Watching two clouds slowly drift apart, she suddenly says, “Some differences are easier to see from a distance.” When Sakaguchi assumes she is analyzing a case again, Iimura smiles and shakes her head. “This time I really am looking at the clouds.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_nurs: Chat with Moe Honjo

Moe Honjo spreads several sticky notes across the table and explains earnestly, “I wanted to write down the little things to remember in the lounge, like washing cups after using them…” She adjusts her glasses, then suddenly laughs. “I suppose that’s something I should already know.”

She sits bolt upright with her cup of water. When Sakaguchi asks why she doesn’t relax, Moe answers quietly, “I keep feeling that if I sit down, I’ll forget what I’m supposed to do next.” Only after looking around does it dawn on her. “Oh, this is where people are supposed to rest.”

Moe studies the steam rising from her cup. “The same cup of water can be too hot for one person and just right for another. Maybe it’s like that when a patient says, ‘It’s all right.’” On this subject, her words suddenly flow easily, and her eyes light up.
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_nur: Chat with Moe Honjo

Standing out of the wind, Moe takes off her glasses to wipe them, then quickly puts them back on. “Wow, I really can’t see anything far away without my glasses.” She smiles and points to a tiny fallen leaf by the wall. “But I do notice little things up close like that quite easily.”

A gust catches a small slip of paper in Moe’s hand, and she hurriedly pins it down. “I-it’s just a reminder I wrote about taking breaks, not an important record!” She folds it into her pocket, then adds earnestly, “Still, I shouldn’t let it blow all over the place.”

Moe looks down at the figures coming and going around the hospital, her voice unusually quiet. “Everyone looks so small from here. But each of them has things to do.” She turns to Sakaguchi and smiles. “Thinking that I can help even a little makes me feel energized.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Emiko Mido

Emiko Mido casually turns a couple of pages in a magazine, then closes it. “The headline sounds very certain, but the article provides little evidence.” She glances at Sakaguchi and sets it down. “Never mind. We needn’t turn the lounge into a discussion meeting.”

As Sakaguchi approaches, Mido doesn’t look up; she simply pulls the chair beside her out a little. “Sit if you want to. You don’t need to stand there waiting for my permission.” After a while, she adds, “If you keep standing there, I can’t read in peace.”

Mido takes a sip of the drink on the table and offers a brief assessment. “The temperature is right. The taste is ordinary.” Sakaguchi asks whether she grades even her breaks. She answers calmly, “I’m not grading it. I’m stating the facts.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Chat with Emiko Mido

Mido stands a little way back from the railing, looking out over the city. “There’s always someone in a hurry downstairs. It’s quiet up here.” She says nothing more until Sakaguchi also looks into the distance, then adds mildly, “Not a bad place.”

The wind ruffles the draft pages in her hands, and Mido holds them firmly down. “Some judgments become clearer with a change of surroundings.” She looks at Sakaguchi, her voice still calm. “But in the end, we must return to the evidence. An elegant idea is no use on its own.”

When Sakaguchi asks whether she wants to be alone, Mido answers frankly, “I only came for a change of perspective.” She glances at him, then turns her gaze back into the distance. “You can stay. You needn’t force yourself to find something to say just to keep me company.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Asuka Shiromiya

Asuka Shiromiya approaches the counter with an empty cup and smiles at Sakaguchi’s greeting. “You don’t have to be so formal here. If everyone keeps calling me Director even in the lounge, I feel as though I ought to sit up perfectly straight.”

Asuka folds away a half-written note. “It always feels as though there’s something left to handle. But if we don’t leave even a little time for breaks, everyone will wear themselves out.” Smiling, she gestures for Sakaguchi to sit. “So let’s talk about something that isn’t in a report.”

Sakaguchi brings up a medical question he is unsure about, and Asuka considers it carefully. “I’d like to check that part further, but I think I know where the key issue lies.” Her smile is a little shy. “Being the director doesn’t mean I can stop learning.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Chat with Asuka Shiromiya

Watching the figures entering and leaving below, Asuka speaks softly. “From here, the hospital seems even bigger than I imagine it when I’m in my office.” She pauses, then smiles. “Not because the building has grown taller. It just makes me think of how many people are here.”

The wind tousles the hair over Asuka’s forehead, and she smooths it back. “Sometimes this is a better place to think than my office. But standing higher doesn’t mean I see everything most clearly.” She turns to Sakaguchi and earnestly asks what he thinks.

She points toward a hospital window visible in the distance. “From outside, it’s just an ordinary room.” Asuka smiles gently. “But the people inside all have their own difficulties. I hope that when they need help, they can actually reach someone.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Artoria Pendragon

Artoria pushes a crooked chair back into place, clearing a path for Sakaguchi. “Of course, there is no need to line up in formation in the lounge.” She looks down at the chair she has just straightened and pauses. “Still, making sure everyone can get through can hardly be a bad thing.”

She sets down the work notice she is holding. When Sakaguchi says she needn’t oversee everything herself, she nods earnestly. “You’re right. If our colleagues can do something well, we should trust them with it.” A moment later, she adds, “That is something I need to practice, too.”

Artoria sits near the door and gestures for Sakaguchi to choose any seat. “No chair here is reserved for someone of higher rank.” Hearing how solemn she sounds, she softens her tone. “Just sit wherever you’re comfortable.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Chat with Artoria Pendragon

Artoria listens quietly to the wind. “Up here, I can hear my own breathing.” Sakaguchi asks whether she gets tired, too, and she nods frankly. “Of course. Acknowledging fatigue is how we know when to rest.”

She studies two roads converging below. “People coming from different directions may still end up together.” Then she gives a small shake of her head. “Sorry. I finally come up for some fresh air, and I start seeing team assignments in the scenery again.”

Sakaguchi jokes that at least no one assigns tasks on the rooftop. Artoria looks up at the sky. “That is a good thing.” She turns back, her expression earnest but relaxed. “If there is something you want to say, I will hear you out. We don’t have to rush to a decision here.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Shiori Fujisaki

Shiori Fujisaki straightens two disheveled magazines into a stack and explains with a smile, “It’s just a habit. Don’t take me for an inspector.” After a moment’s thought, she adds frankly, “Though if it were a contest to see who could arrange them most neatly, I probably wouldn’t want to lose.”

Sakaguchi asks what she would like to talk about now that she has a moment free. Shiori considers it carefully, then smiles. “Let’s talk about something outside the hospital. We can sort patients’ symptoms into categories, but people’s feelings won’t always fit into a tidy table.”

Shiori turns her cup with her fingertips. “Sometimes I think first about how to say something so it won’t be misunderstood.” She looks at Sakaguchi with a slightly mischievous smile. “But if you think I’m being too serious, you’ll have to give me a good reason.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Chat with Shiori Fujisaki

Shiori Fujisaki looks at the sky beyond the railing. “This is a good place for a quiet moment.” When Sakaguchi asks whether she dislikes lively company, she smiles and shakes her head. “Not really. It’s just that sometimes, if I don’t rush to answer, I can work out what I truly want to say.”

A breeze passes, and Shiori tucks her hair behind her ear. “When there are several ways to do something, I always want to find the best one.” She tilts her head with a smile. “But hearing other people’s reasons can sometimes be more interesting than rushing to win.”

Looking at the neatly aligned rooftops in the distance, Shiori suddenly laughs. “I’m usually so intent on doing things better that I nearly started comparing the scenery.” She turns to Sakaguchi. “At least up here, I can stop ranking things for a while.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Minato Haruka

Minato Haruka looks at the assortment of cups on the rack and smiles. “People’s little habits show even when they’re resting. It’s rather interesting. I often remember how someone likes to put their cup away faster than I remember where I left my own.”

She shifts her chair to make room for Sakaguchi. “You don’t look as though you want to hear a medical report. Come and sit for a bit, then.” Her voice is easy, but she still remembers to ask, “Would you like some water? I can get you some while I’m at it.”

Minato pats the pocket of her white coat, then notices the note she is looking for sitting on the table. “Oh, there it is.” She picks it up with a laugh. “I can never keep track of little things like this. Luckily, the cases that really matter have proper records; they don’t depend on where I stuff my scraps of paper.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Chat with Minato Haruka

Minato watches the stream of people outside the hospital. “It’s the little worries patients have that tend to stick with me. Being afraid someone will mispronounce their name, for instance, or not liking other people to answer for them.” She smiles. “The numbers on a calendar, on the other hand, often seem to have it in for me.”

The wind is a little chilly. Minato studies Sakaguchi’s expression. “If you want to talk, I can listen. If you just want to stand here, that’s fine, too.” She smiles lazily. “The nice thing about the rooftop is that no one insists we find something to talk about.”

Minato points to a stretch of road in the distance. “It’s quite easy to get your bearings from here.” Sakaguchi asks whether she gets lost as well, and she waves the idea away with a laugh. “Not on the roads. The time we agreed to meet, though… You’d better write that down clearly for me.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Aqua Mizuki

Aqua Mizuki gestures toward the sofa a couple of times and says enthusiastically, “You know, feeling comfortable sitting on something is completely different from actually lying down on it!” Seeing Sakaguchi’s expression, she immediately laughs. “Don’t worry, I’m not planning to experiment on the lounge sofa.”

Aqua spends a while studying the buttons on the drinks machine. “Why are some options always in the most prominent positions? Could that affect what people choose?” Sakaguchi assumes she has thought of another new device, but she waves it off. “No! Let me study something that doesn’t need a paper written about it once in a while.”

She sits down with a few draft pages, rattles off three explanations, then rejects two of them herself. Seeing that Sakaguchi can’t keep up, Aqua laughs heartily. “It’s all right, I’m sorting out my thoughts. When I’m actually explaining things to a patient, of course I take it one sentence at a time!”
Chat with Sakura

Sakura quietly moves her chair toward a peaceful corner and glances up at Sakaguchi. “I’m not avoiding you. It’s quieter here.” She pauses. “If we’re going to talk about work, let me finish this water first.”

Sakaguchi asks whether Sakura dislikes jokes. She sets down her cup. “I like them. In the right setting.” Seeing that he is still waiting for more, she adds without a change of expression, “You’re not standing beside the operating table now. Go on.”

Sakura watches the lounge clock for a moment, then suddenly says, “Time seems to pass more slowly when it’s quiet.” Just as Sakaguchi is about to answer, she adds, “Don’t worry. I’m not planning to put that in the anesthesia record.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_nurs: Chat with Satsuki Orikawa

When Satsuki Orikawa sees Sakaguchi come in, she instinctively adjusts her glasses. “M-Mr. Sakaguchi, are you taking a break, too?” She quickly moves aside, only to notice that there are other empty chairs. Her voice grows quieter. “I just wanted you to be comfortable…”

Looking at a hospital leaflet on the table, she says softly, “It says, ‘Please don’t worry,’ but perhaps patients would rather know exactly what happens next.” As she turns to specific nursing matters, her speech becomes steadier. “Explaining what we’re going to do first makes it easier for people to feel at ease.”

Sakaguchi notices that Satsuki has placed her cup well away from the door. A little embarrassed, she explains, “Fewer people pass by there, so the cup is less likely to get knocked over.” After a brief pause, she adds earnestly, “It’s the same in the ward. Little things affect how safe people feel.”
strings.ui.event.whole_sunday: This date takes the whole Sunday. Finish to begin the next workday.
strings.collections.character_events.sayaka_week: A workday morning. Sakaguchi has just put down a patient's chart when Sayaka knocks on his open office door, a consultation form in hand.
“Thanks. I've already seen you in two departments this morning. How come you're over here now?”
“I go wherever they need someone. All right, save your thanks. Sign here.”
She taps the last page with her pen. Clearly, she has already found the place for his signature.
“You look like you're here to collect a debt.”
Once Sakaguchi signs, she checks it and puts the papers away.
“For this one. You've probably got more to do today, but I'm not keeping track for you.”
She reaches the door, then stops as if something has just occurred to her.
“Your number. I wouldn't have any use for your phone.”
Sayaka opens her contacts and looks up at him.
“Aren't you worried I might get the wrong idea?”
“You can get a little bit of the wrong idea for now. Your number?”
Sakaguchi gives her his number. She quickly types it in and sends the first message.
Sakaguchi saves the contact on his phone. Sayaka leans over from beside the desk to peek at the screen.
“Hey, wait. You're not really saving me as 'Dr. Nanjo,' are you? It looks like a hospital mailing list.”
She answers so quickly that she gives herself pause. Their eyes meet; she glances away first, then smiles.
“...Don't actually change it yet. We're not that close.”
“It rolled off your tongue pretty easily just now.”
“Just letting you know the option exists.”
Can I message you at two in the morning?
“Oh, please. I'm just worried you'll actually change it, say it out loud at the hospital, and the whole nurses' station will know.”
“Sounds like you're more worried about them finding out.”
“Give that lot a scrap of gossip and they'll talk about it for three days. It's still too early for that.”
“I never said that. Whether you can message me outside work—why don't you try and find out?”
“So it depends on what I send.”
“Exactly. You can't expect me to come up with your first message for you.”
“Can I message you at two in the morning?”
“No boring messages at two in the morning. I have work the next day.”
“I can't promise I'll have the patience for questions in the middle of the night.”
“You send the first one. I'll be the judge.”
She slips her phone into her white coat pocket, takes two steps out, then looks back.
“Like... asking if I'm off work yet. That sort of thing.”
“Aren't you busy right up until the end of the day too?”
“That's why I want you to ask. All right, back to work.”
Sayaka leaves the office. For the first time, Sakaguchi has a contact on his phone he might use after work.
strings.collections.character_events.sayaka_lv1_: Sunday. There are no regular outpatient appointments or elective operations. Sakaguchi opens the contact he saved earlier.
“Free today? Want to get something to eat?”
A few seconds later, another message arrives.
“Oh, so you're picking me this Sunday?”
Sakaguchi sends the address. Before long, she sends a brief confirmation. They agree to meet outside the restaurant that afternoon.
Sakaguchi arrives a few minutes early. A familiar figure is already waiting outside. Sayaka is in casual clothes, her hair falling naturally, without her hospital white coat.
“By two minutes. Don't make it sound like I've been standing here pining for you.”
“I was worried I'd keep you waiting.”
“It's two minutes. It's not my first time going out to eat on my own.”
She looks at the sign by the door, then through the window at the tables for two under the warm lights.
“You know how to pick a place. This could easily give someone the wrong idea.”
“That you're asking me on a date.”
“Weren't you the one who said it was just a meal?”
“You said 'just' first. Come on, let's go in. Keep discussing this in the doorway and the staff will think we're arguing.”
She pushes the door open and goes in first, turning to wait for Sakaguchi only when she reaches the table. She seems perfectly at ease with company.
They sit down. A server brings menus and water, then leaves.
“It's kind of novel seeing you outside the hospital.”
She looks down at her clothes, then back at Sakaguchi.
You look great like this too
I'm still getting used to it
“A little. A white coat suits you.”
“Only just noticed? Not very observant, Dr. Sakaguchi.”
“I said it suits you, not that it's the only thing you look good in.”
“Oh, so you know how to leave yourself an escape route. Fine, you're off the hook for now.”
Sayaka is about to look back down at the menu, but pauses.
She lowers her head, but the smile lingers at the corners of her mouth.
“I'm still getting used to it. I see you in a white coat every day at work.”
“Take your time. You'll have more chances.”
Suddenly realizing how much that sounds like she has already arranged a next time, she presses her lips together.
The server returns to ask whether they have decided. At last, they turn their attention back to the menus.
“The menu here looks pretty good. Any recommendations?”
“It's my first time here. I only checked the location and opening hours. We'll have to take our chances with the food.”
“You're actually admitting that? I thought you'd say you'd done your homework.”
“I can't pretend to be an expert on Italian food in front of you. Do you come to places like this often?”
“Now and then. After a week of cafeteria food, I want something different on Sunday. Hmm... that seafood pasta looks good.”
“After all that deliberation, you're still going with pasta?”
“What's wrong with ordering pasta at an Italian restaurant? It's not like I can order a convenience-store rice ball.”
After ordering, Sayaka closes her menu and puts it aside. Rather than rushing to find a new topic, she takes a sip of water and watches people pass outside.
“Is this how you usually spend Sundays?”
“Sleep in, wander around, eat whatever I feel like. Sometimes I come alone. That's nice too.”
“With your personality, I thought you'd spend weekends meeting a big group of friends.”
“I do that too. But when you talk to people all day, some time alone feels good. What, do you think I have to find someone to talk to the moment I'm free?”
“Not exactly. I just always see you running around at work.”
“Running around at work is work. Sitting here on a Sunday is a day off. You've got to keep the two separate.”
They both laugh. When the first dish arrives, she takes a bite and pays close attention to the taste.
“Mm, this really is good. Nice choice of restaurant.”
“Didn't you just say I hadn't done my homework?”
“Picking the right place without doing your homework? That's good luck, then.”
This time, instead of teasing him further, she naturally turns the conversation to Sakaguchi himself.
“By the way, since coming to Hoshimi, have you been anywhere besides the hospital?”
“Not really. Hospital during the day, charts at night. At most, I pick up something to eat after work.”
“That explains it. I was wondering why even choosing a place for a weekend meal felt like scheduling a consultation.”
“Does that mean I need to submit a summary report today too?”
“No. I'm not wearing a white coat today. No reports.”
She twirls a forkful of pasta, her smile a little more relaxed than it is at the hospital.
“Still, I'm a little surprised. You know everyone at the hospital, yet you remember what I said when I first arrived.”
“Why wouldn't I? I remember people I enjoy talking to. Patient charts aren't the only things worth remembering.”
“So far. You've been serious about your work these past few days, and you don't only talk about yourself. Sitting here with you, I don't feel like I have to keep finding things to say.”
“You found quite a lot just now.”
“I like chatting. That's not the same as being afraid of silence.”
Sakaguchi looks at her. Sayaka notices, but doesn't immediately reach for another joke.
“For a while there, you were just enjoying your food. It's different from how you are at the hospital.”
“Of course. This dish is good. Am I supposed to stay in doctor mode even after work?”
“I like this too. You look happy.”
For half a second, Sayaka has no reply. She looks down, puts her fork aside, and smiles faintly.
“...Yeah. I am having a good time today.”
The conversation rests there for a moment. The light outside has grown warmer since they sat down.
“Then can I ask something a bit more personal?”
“You've already asked me out to eat, and you're still afraid to ask questions?”
“Do you usually say yes to men this easily?”
She answers frankly, then takes a more thoughtful look at Sakaguchi.
“But I don't go out with just anyone who asks. If I'm having a meal with someone I've only known for a few days, I at least have to find him interesting.”
“We haven't even finished eating. What's the rush? Eat your food.”
She laughs first and finishes the last of her pasta. Sakaguchi doesn't press the question.

The main course is finished. Sayaka glances over the dessert menu and eventually orders a small treat. By the time the plates are cleared, it has begun to grow dark outside. Their conversation drifts from the hospital to nearby shops, then slowly back to today.
Sayaka gently turns her empty glass with her fingertips, without immediately making a joke as she did before.
I just came out for a meal
Sayaka pauses for a beat and looks up at him.
“What else? I wanted to spend time alone with you today.”
She picks up her glass but doesn't drink right away, simply smiling at Sakaguchi.
She answers quickly. This time, Sakaguchi is the one who looks at her for a moment.
“I'm already here. Why pretend? So, what about you?”
She looks down and smiles, as though pleased to have finally put something obvious into words.
“I just came out for a meal.”
Sayaka is still smiling when she hears Sakaguchi's answer. She hesitates slightly.
She looks down at her plate, her smile fading a little.
“Then I'll try a little harder next time.”
“Making it feel more like a date.”
“...Then why did you say it was just a meal?”
“That really was what I thought when I left home.”
“But after spending this time with you, I've changed my mind a little.”
She looks at Sakaguchi, her disappointment gradually turning into a smile.
“...Honestly. Why do you only find the right words at a time like this?”
“So, does today count as a date?”
“But say it sooner next time. Don't make me ask everything first.”
They smile at each other, and the atmosphere relaxes again.
The server brings the bill. Just as Sakaguchi reaches for it, Sayaka already has her card out.
Seeing Sakaguchi's slight surprise, she smiles first.
“Hey, don't overthink it. I'm not drawing a line, and I'm not saying 'we're just friends.'”
“That's why I'm saying it now. This is how I date.”
“Yes. We each pay our own way.”
She puts her card on the table, waits for the server to collect the bill, then winks at Sakaguchi.
“As for the rest... we'll talk about that later.”
Sakaguchi can't help laughing too. They settle the bill and walk out of the restaurant side by side.
A few shops are still lit along the evening street. The station is only a short walk away, but Sayaka doesn't head toward its entrance right away.
“How high a score do you want?”
“At least enough for a next time?”
“Of course. Why else would I have said 'we'll talk about that later'?”
Sakaguchi thinks she is about to say goodbye, but Sayaka looks down the road ahead.
“Let's walk a little farther. We're not in a hurry today.”
They walk slowly along the street. This time, she doesn't rush to take the lead in conversation, listening as Sakaguchi talks about streets he hasn't had time to explore yet.
“Because it feels pretty good when someone you like takes the initiative.”
After saying it, she briefly looks away, then quickly regains her usual expression.
“Is that your way of giving me an answer?”
“Haven't I always been direct? All right, don't let it go to your head.”
At the corner where they part, Sayaka turns to wave and heads toward the station. Sakaguchi watches her walk away before turning toward home.
On a workday after their first date, Sakaguchi meets Sayaka in the corridor, carrying a stack of charts.
“Morning. Don't forget your consultation this afternoon. I left the materials on your desk.”
“We're at work now. Nobody said on our date that we'd stop doing our jobs at the hospital.”
“What about the next time we talked about?”
Her steps slow for half a beat, and she smiles at him.
“I'm waiting. Come find me once you've picked a place.”
“Didn't you do well last time? All right, I've still got charts to deliver.”
She shifts the files to her other arm and continues down the corridor like any other colleague. After two steps, she turns back for one small glance.

strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_abd: Wait—! That whole thing being pulled out from inside just now... Was that my uterus?!

strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_vag: Ah—! It hurts! You've really started cutting down there?!

Ah— wait! Something deep inside keeps being pulled downward... Is that my uterus?!

strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_dis: Ah... Something inside suddenly pulled so painfully... Are you cutting through my stomach now?!
Wait! After this cut, a piece of my stomach will really be gone, won't it?!
It hurts... Don't just say 'resection complete'... That's my stomach...
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_tot: Wait—! You've cut through the esophagus too now?! Does that mean my entire stomach is detached?!
Ah... It hurts so much... Don't say 'total gastrectomy complete'... I can hear you...
You've removed all of it?! I really don't have a stomach anymore?!
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_nep: Wait... That thing you just took away... Was that really my kidney?!
You've cut the whole thing out already?! Do I really only have the other one left now?!
Ah... Don't call it a specimen... That came out of my body...
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_par: It hurts—! You're cutting out the tumor, right?! Not the whole kidney?!
Wait! The normal kidney is still there, right? Don't cut it out along with it...
Ah... It hurts so much... First tell me you're cutting out the lesion, not the whole kidney...
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_liv: Wait... That huge piece you just lifted away... Was that really my liver?!
Ah... You really cut away that much?!
Don't say 'liver lobe specimen'... It sounds so frightening... That was part of my body just a moment ago...
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_cab: It hurts so much... Wait! Did you just say you're going to stop my heart?!

strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_aaa: Ah... Wait! Did you just say you're going to clamp my aorta?! Now?!

strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_lob: Wait! Are you cutting the bronchus to that lung lobe now?!

Don't say it so calmly... After this cut, the whole lung will really be detached, won't it?!
What you just lifted away... Was that really an entire lung?!

Don't let me see! Don't put that thing where I can see it... That's my lung...
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_eso: Wait?! You aren't finished with my abdomen, and now you're opening my chest too?!
Ah... What do you mean, 'move to the chest'?! You're making another incision in my chest?!
N-no, haven't you already opened my abdomen... Why are you opening my chest now too...?!
Ah... Wait! Are you cutting through my esophagus now?!
This end has to be cut through too?! Then you're really going to connect a stomach tube to it?!
It hurts... I heard you say 'proximal division'... Don't act like I don't understand!
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_rad: Wait... That thing you just took away... Was that my bladder?!
You've cut the whole thing out already?! Does that mean I'll really never use my own bladder again?!
Ah... Don't say 'specimen'... That was still inside my body just a moment ago...
Wait... Are you making a new opening for urine on my abdomen now?!
Ah... You're really fixing the stoma in place right here already?!
D-don't keep saying 'mature the stoma'... I know I'll pass urine through here from now on, but hearing it now is so embarrassing...
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_apr: Ah—!! Wait! You've really started cutting between my legs?! Stop a moment, it hurts too much!
There... Right in that embarrassing place between my anus and vagina, you're really cutting inward?! I can feel it!
It hurts... So much... D-don't all crowd between my legs to do this... I know it's surgery, but it's so embarrassing...
Ah— wait! Something inside is being pulled all the way down between my legs... What is that?!
You're really pulling that whole section out from the anal side?! It hurts so much...!
D-don't say 'it's out'... That feeling of something being pulled all the way out from so far below... I really don't want to know what it was...
You're still stitching between my legs, and making a stoma on my abdomen too... Why aren't you finished on either side yet?!
It hurts... You're still stitching down there, and the stoma's already fixed in place too?!
Don't talk about finishing the stitches down there and the stoma at the same time... I can hear everything. It's so embarrassing...
strings.collections.awake_special_barks.noan_lar: Ah—! So deep... Wait, are you cutting through something really low inside my abdomen now?!
You're already that close to the inside of my anus?! D-don't go any lower...
It hurts... That last bit was deep inside, really low down, wasn't it?! You really can still preserve my anus, can't you?!
Ah... There's pressure inside again... Are you joining the two ends deep above my anus now?!
It hurts... That spot is so deep and so low... You're reconnecting it inside there right now?!
Wait... I know you're reconstructing it, but I can feel it so clearly there... Stop saying 'a little lower'...
strings.patient_dialogue_profiles.playful_defian: “Huh, I need to stay in the hospital? This is getting serious... How long will I be here?”
“All right, I'll stay. But if there's anything I don't understand, I'm going to ask.”
“Wait, that isn't what you said earlier, is it? Doctor, just because I'm lying here doesn't mean I wasn't listening.”
“Mm, that's much clearer now. Thank you for explaining it to me.”
“Huh? That's all? Tell me a little more. I'm the one this is happening to.”
“All right, I'll cooperate... But you have to keep talking to me, too.”
“Sleeping through it sounds pretty nice... But going to sleep without knowing anything is still a little scary.”
“My body will be numb, but my head will stay clear? Hmm... Then I'll hear everything you say.”
“Local anesthesia... If I tell you it hurts, you'll listen, right?”
“Huh? No anesthesia?! Doctor, I didn't come here for a pain-endurance contest.”
“Mm... I'm counting on you, then. This time I'm really putting myself in your hands.”
“No! I said I'd cooperate, not that I could stand being cut open without anesthesia!”
“D-don't just tell me to hold still! It hurts so much my whole body wants to pull away...!”
“Hold me steady... Even with the anesthetic, I'm still shaking from nerves.”
“My legs aren't really doing what I tell them anymore... You'd better hold me steady.”
“Ngh... Have you started? It doesn't hurt as much as I imagined, but knowing you're really operating is still so frightening...”
“Ah...! I can feel you moving... H-have you already started cutting?”
“Aaah!! It hurts! It really hurts! W-wait... I can't take it anymore...!”
“Thank you... I almost couldn't bear it just then. Let me catch my breath...”
“All right, I'll stay still... But if I can't help crying out, you're not allowed to laugh at me.”
“W-wait! You're just going to keep going? At least answer me...!”
“Mm, I'm listening. When you tell me what you're doing, I don't keep imagining things.”
“Ha... You're finally looking at me. I thought all you could see was the surgical field.”
“Doctor? Why has everyone suddenly gone quiet...? I'm still awake.”
“It's really almost over? Whew... I shouldn't have talked so tough earlier.”
“Breathe slowly... All right, I'll follow your rhythm.”
“It's almost done, right...? Tell me, Doctor... I'll worry.”
“Oh, an enema? That's part of the preparation, too... Wait, right now?”
“Mm, lie on my side... All right. I never thought being hospitalized would mean needing help even with this.”
“Huh? Isn't this step optional? Then why do it?”
“Doing it anyway when it isn't needed? Doctor, this isn't trying out a new menu.”
“All right, I won't pull away... Wait, you have to shave that far down, too?!”
“Skin preparation, right... Huh? Here, too? How can you all act so matter-of-fact about it...?”
“You have to shave places that aren't being operated on, too? ...That's a little strange, isn't it?”
“Huh? Skin preparation outside the surgical area? Doctor, tell me why first.”
“All my hair goes inside? All right... I really look like a surgical patient now.”
“Hey, can you still recognize me like this? Don't mix me up with someone else!”
“My legs go here... Mm, I know I've had anesthetic, but I'm still awake.”
“Wait, don't suddenly turn me over. I'm awake; tell me first.”
“You're securing me before giving any anesthesia? W-wait... What if it hurts so much I can't help moving?”
“I have to stay like this even after you start cutting...? Doctor, I suddenly don't feel like laughing at all...”
“A urinary catheter... Mm, I understand. But putting it in there... It's really rather embarrassing.”
“How can you all be so calm at a time like this...? All right, I'll try not to move.”
“Ah...! W-wait... That's so uncomfortable! I'm completely awake...!”
“D-don't put it in without warning! Tell me first... I really will flinch if you startle me!”
“Ooh, that's cold! So I can still feel the cold disinfectant even after the anesthetic.”
“You've disinfected all the way here... The scalpel is next, isn't it? Tell me before you start.”
“So cold... Wait, once the disinfecting is done, you're really going straight to cutting?”
“It's only disinfectant... But thinking of the cut that's coming next already has me trembling...”
“Oh, this is the incision... Even with anesthesia, I can't help wanting to look.”
“Do you start once you've finished marking? I may still be smiling, but I'm really a little nervous.”
“You're really going to cut straight along this line? Without anesthesia... Are you serious...?”
“Don't make me keep staring at it... Thinking of the knife cutting along here scares me...”

strings.collections.character_events.ange_lv1_ha: An Qi reorganized the three scattered remarks into one sentence.
——Epilogue: The next day, the nurse’s station.

Seeing Sakaguchi, she took the initiative to say hello.
"Good morning. Bed Six was in stable condition last night."
An Qi reorganized the three scattered remarks into one sentence.
Angel was still confirming the shift handover details after get off work.
Sakaguchi has finished his ward rounds and is preparing to leave the ward.
Next to the nurse's station, An Qi was holding the shift record and explaining the situation to the taking over nurse.
"Six beds need to pay attention to their eating tonight. I only ate less than half of my lunch. I didn't feel sick in the afternoon, but I didn't drink much water."
The taking over nurse marked the record.
"Okay, I understand. I'll do the rest."
"Also, when he says he feels discomfort in his abdomen, he will first say, 'Maybe I'm too sensitive.' You can ask more."
An Qi handed the record out and took it back.
"By the way, the family members brought it——"
"Dr. Sakaguchi. Are there any new medical orders for bed six?"
"No. What time do you get off work?"
She glanced at the clock on the wall.
"She's done it once. This is the second time."
Angel's ears are a little red.
"I missed some details the first time."
Sakaguchi took the record and looked at it.
The handwriting is neat, and several easily overlooked places are marked in different colors. There was a small rabbit sticker stuck to the corner of the paper, which she folded in half.
She realized that Sakaguchi had seen it, and subconsciously stretched out her hand to press the corner of the paper.
SakaguchiReturn the record to the relief nurse.
"I understand the situation of the six beds. If there are changes at night, please contact us according to the on-duty arrangements."
"When he says it's okay...it doesn't necessarily mean it's okay."
The taking over nurse shook the record in her hand.
"I remember it. He first said, 'Maybe I'm too sensitive,' so I asked one more question."
An Qi looked at her, then at Sakaguchi, and finally nodded.
——Transition: at the entrance of the hospital.
An Qi changed into casual clothes and came out, carrying a small bag on her shoulder that was much lighter than when working. When she saw Sakaguchi, her steps slowed down.
She looked down at her phone and the screen lit up.
"The next one is in seven minutes."
The two of them walked along the way to the station.
An Qi walked for a while and suddenly asked:
"Am I too long-winded in my shift handover?"
"Some things can be sorted out in advance. The one about six beds is worth talking about."
An Qi put her mobile phone into her bag, moved the corners of her mouth, and quickly returned to her normal appearance.
When she reached the intersection, she glanced at the bus stop and suddenly quickened her pace.
She had walked out and stopped again.
She trotted into the convenience store and the bell on the door rang.
Angel was still confirming the shift handover details after get off work.
strings.collections.character_events.ange_lv2_ex: On the day of surgery, she kept her promise to accompany the patient in.

After she finished speaking, she added:
Angel squeezed the cookie bag loudly.
"I'm afraid she'll ask me something that I don't even know."
"Then I got busy and couldn't care less about it."
She lowered her head and picked out an unbroken cookie and handed it to Sakaguchi.
An Qi looked at the remaining broken cookies in her hand and suddenly smiled softly.
"The answers I prepared last night are useless today."
On the day of surgery, she kept her promise to accompany the patient in.
Angel prepared all the answers, but encountered the question that the patient was really afraid of.
When Sakaguchi walked into the ward, An Qi was explaining the arrangements for the next day to an adult female patient.
She was so well prepared that she barely had to look down at the information.

"The ward nurse will accompany you tomorrow morning. After entering the surgery area, we will check your identity and surgery information again. Your belongings can be handed over to your family members for safekeeping first—"

"Do you have anything else to ask?"
"Then please prepare according to the requirements just explained tonight. If there is any-"
The patient clutched the corners of the quilt.
"We will always have someone with you. The anesthesiologist has also talked to you about this operation-"
"I'm sorry, I just couldn't help it."
An Qi lowered her head and glanced at the information. The answers to the above questions that may be asked have already been written.
"Which part are you most afraid of now?"
The patient hesitated for a moment.
"Everyone knows what to do. Only I don't know. I'm afraid I won't even know where to lie down by then."
An Qi raised her eyes. The patient smiled again, this time more embarrassed.
"You don't have to remember that. When tomorrow comes, I'll tell you what to do next."
She looked back at the patient.

An Qi pulled out the small card tucked into the information. It contains the order of explanations she has arranged in advance, and the last line is: confirm patient understanding and answer questions.
As soon as the words came out of her mouth, she felt a little regretful. Sakaguchi didn't smile.
"You just said what she needs most tomorrow."
An Qi looked at the ward door. After a while, she wrote a few words on the back of the card and put it back in her pocket.
Angel prepared all the answers, but encountered the question that the patient was really afraid of.
strings.collections.character_events.ange_lv3_ch: An Qi took the initiative to try to schedule the next surgery.
——Epilogue: The next day, in front of the schedule.

"Sugimura-senpai, can I use this one with Dr. Sakaguchi?"
"So there are still some places that I want to learn again."
Hiroko made a mark on the watch.
An Qi thanked her, took a few steps, and then came back.
"Um...please don't say it was my special request."
An Qi straightened the record folder a little.
An Qi took the initiative to try to schedule the next surgery.
Angel asked Sakaguchi to confirm again before closing.
A common abdominal surgery is coming to an end.
Angel serves as the device nurse for Sakaguchi today. Several transfers were made slightly earlier than Sakaguchi. The operation went smoothly and her tight shoulders gradually relaxed.
When the final inspection before closing began, she suddenly spoke:
"The color that was attracted just now is darker than the previous one. I'm worried that there is still bleeding."
"It's not much, but I think we should recheck the location we just dealt with."
Sakaguchi looked at the field of surgery.
"No new bleeding has been seen so far."
The voice suddenly became louder. An Qi realized it herself and immediately lowered her voice.
"Okay. Tell me again the order you just saw."
An Qi was stunned for a moment and began to report. After Sakaguchi listened, he took her to confirm again.
There was no new active bleeding. What I saw just now was the residual blood, which was brought out with the flushing.
Sakaguchi motioned for her to see clearly.
"What's the difference between here and the situation you're worried about?"
An Qi observed carefully for a while.
"There is no continued leakage. There is no re-accumulation after flushing."
"You're right when you see the color getting darker. The cause was determined a little early."
Sakaguchi continues to complete the check.
An Qi was quieter than usual as she sorted out the records. When Sakaguchi came back, he found that she had not left yet.
"Is there something that doesn't match up?"
"I'm sorry for wasting your time just now."
"But you have already judged it. I still insist on it."
Sakaguchi pulled up a chair and sat down.
"What do you think we should do next time?"
An Qi thought for a while.
"Confirm my judgment first, and then report to you."
"How long does it take to confirm?"
"What if by the time you finish confirming, the situation has changed?"
"Tell me what you see. You can also tell me what you think it is. If you can't tell it clearly at the moment, just tell me that you can't tell it."
Ange looked down at the edge of the clip.
"I think a good assistant should be able to give the doctor an accurate answer."
"Of course it's good to be accurate. But when I ask you about your situation, I'm not taking a test."
"You don't have to wait until you are sure to get full marks before you speak."
An Qi seemed to want to retort, but finally just took a breath.
Sakaguchi stood up and prepared to see the patient. When she reached the door, she called to him again.
"If I still feel something is wrong next time, I will ask you to stop."
Only then did An Qi smile a little.
Angel asked Sakaguchi to confirm again before closing.
strings.collections.character_events.ange_lv4_af: After the emergency call at night, An Qi admitted for the first time that she was scared just now.

What Sakaguchi wants is right in front of you. She knows.

She swallowed back what she was about to say and nodded slightly.

She let go of the tissue she had been clutching.
When Sakaguchi came back, she had washed her face and combed her hair again.
But after seeing him, she didn't stand up straight as usual.
She picked up her bag and walked over to him.
"Can you walk a little slower today?"
After the emergency call at night, An Qi admitted for the first time that she was scared just now.
strings.collections.character_events.ange_lv5_ca: The patient remembered Angel's voice, and she also said her next request.

In the middle of the operation, the actual situation was more complicated than the preoperative judgment.

Admit that I paid too much attention
Ask her to review the medical history together.

At the outpatient table, Shiori placed Sakaguchi's preoperative records of the three recent surgeries, this consultation sheet, and the patient's long-term medication list side by side, and pointed to one of the blank spaces.
"The treatment of the first three cases was all stable. However, this time, although the plan for the lesion was clear, her recent shortness of breath when going upstairs was not included in the preoperative judgment."
Smiling and bringing the topic back to the consultation sheet

"Thank you. Actually, it's not a secret that must be hidden. It's just that every time I'm recognized, I don't know which expression to put on."
Her smile slowly became natural.
"People in the entertainment industry are very kind to me, but there are always people there who want me to be 'Shiori Fujisaki' in their minds. How to laugh today, what to say, who to like... I have never been used to it."
She tapped the consultation sheet on the table with her fingertips.
"Medicine is not easy, but at least what patients need is not a designed role. They need me to listen carefully, clarify the problem, and then admit what I can and cannot do."
"So, it's more comfortable to be a doctor. Although when I was working the night shift, I occasionally doubted the choice I made back then."
Accept this consultation partner

"There is one more thing I need to explain first."
She looked at the consultation sheet, her tone still gentle.
"If I think that my overall condition is not suitable for surgery, I will explicitly ask for a postponement. Even if you or Dr. Mido are the surgeon, it will be the same."
After saying that, she showed a subtle smile.
"I hope that the first time we disagreed, we could explain the reasons clearly like we did today."
So you finally chose medicine?
Don't worry, I won't publicize this everywhere.

"The national goddess of the country..."
Shiori was very calm just now, but when she heard this title, she visibly stiffened. She subconsciously touched the hairband, and the tips of her ears turned red.
"Please don't use such exaggerated titles in the hospital. If a patient hears it, I might have to sign 'National Goddess Doctor' on the medical record tomorrow."
She coughed slightly and tried to regain her usual dignified tone.
"I did participate in a game character design audition. I thought it was a fun souvenir at first, but then... it became a bit bigger. Advertisements, interviews, invitations from agencies, all came."
The name sounds familiar...have you been to the draft before?
Wait... aren't you the "national goddess" Shiori Fujisaki?

"It's normal for a surgeon to look at the lesion first. The point of medical consultation is to pull the camera back a little."
Shiori did not show off the conclusion, but only rearranged the symptoms, medications and previous examinations according to time.
"Beautiful individual data are reassuring, but patients are not a data table. If you have any cases in the future where the preoperative risks are uncertain, please come to me directly."

It's good to hear that the operation was successful

It turned out to be the nurse from yesterday

Wait for her to respond

she stopped me

Take note of her research contact details

"Yes. Fear, Pain, Dignity, Cooperation - not four unrelated slots. As long as you find the trigger point, your body will tell you how they are connected."

"If there are any strange cases in the future, please remember to call me. The more incomprehensible the explanation, the better."
"This would explain many of the perioperative reactions."

introduce yourself to her

introduce yourself to her

wait for her reaction

Let her change clothes first

Our eyes met.

keep facing the wall

She falls silent for a long moment, then touches her lower belly.
“Since you are already opening me up...”
“Could you get rid of a little of the extra fat here while you are at it?”
She goes silent again for two seconds.
“...Never mind. Pretend I said nothing.”
She suddenly pulls her abdomen in tight.
A few seconds later, she realizes that makes no sense.
“...Would this make it easier to operate?”
She slowly lets out her breath.
“What am I even trying to help with...?”
Her face rapidly turns pale.
“I saw this in a movie once...”
She seems to be trying desperately to stop herself from thinking any further.
“You really will be able to see my intestines and everything, right?”
“No. The picture is already in my head.”
She goes completely still.
“Open surgery...”
Looking down at her abdomen, she traces a finger from her upper belly to her lower belly.
“How... long will the incision be?”
“You are not going to open my whole stomach, are you...?”
She nods, then suddenly seems to remember something.
“Wait.”
“...Where do you go in?”
“You are not going in through the nipple, are you...?”
The image in her own head clearly frightens her.
“...You have to cut my breast?”
She looks down at herself.
“You are not going to slice straight through the middle like a watermelon, are you...?”
“...No, at this size it would be more like a peach.”

She covers her face.
“What am I even thinking right now...?”
She stares down at her chest for a long moment.
“...Will both sides still be the same size afterward?”
Without thinking, she cups her breasts.
“Why have I never seriously compared them before?”
“Of course I only start worrying about this when I need surgery...”
Her face turns pale, yet the first thing she says is:
“If I had known, I would not have worn this bra today...”
She freezes as soon as the words leave her mouth.
“...No. Those things have absolutely nothing to do with each other.”
“Great. I really am scared senseless.”
She presses a hand to her chest without thinking.
“So... you really will see my heart?”
“It will be beating right in front of you...”
Her expression grows complicated.
“That feels so strange. Just imagining it is a little embarrassing.”
She makes herself sit up straight.
“It is all right.”
“I am not afraid.”
She nods with great conviction.
Three seconds later, she asks, “...Do you really have to saw through my breastbone?”
“I am sorry.”
“I know you just explained everything very clearly.”
She pauses.
“But it feels as if none of it stayed in my head.”
“All that is left is: ‘I am going to have surgery.’”
She is silent for a long time.
“It is not a figure of speech.”
“You really are going to operate on me.”
She looks at the doctor as though only now has she understood what all the previous explanations meant.
She keeps nodding with great seriousness.
“Yes, I understand.”
After several seconds of silence, she speaks in a small voice.
“Afterward, when I... do that, I will not be able to feel that something inside was moved before, will I?”

She immediately covers her face.
“Why was that the first thing I thought of...?”
Her face slowly turns red.
“So... you will see a place very deep inside me.”
She falls silent for a moment.
“Even my boyfriend could never see that far inside...”

The instant she says it, her whole body freezes.
“...Did I just say something really strange?”
She stares blankly for a moment.
“You will be able to see my ovaries too...”
“What do they actually look like again?”
“They do not really look like two grapes, do they...?”
She mutters under her breath, “Why am I thinking about this now?”
She places a hand over her lower abdomen.
“Your uterus is something you normally cannot feel at all.”
“Then suddenly someone tells you they have to open your abdomen and touch it.”
She is quiet for a moment.
“I do not know why. It suddenly feels so private.”
Her body visibly stiffens.
“The pelvis...”
Her voice grows quieter.
“Do you... go in from below?”

When she hears that this operation requires an abdominal incision, she still does not look relieved.
“...Why are both possibilities so frightening?”
She tries to nod, then seems to realize something.
“Once you are inside... you really can see my uterus, right?”
“Would you ever... take it out to look at it?”
Her face immediately turns red.
“I did not mean take it out for a tour!”
Without thinking, she raises both hands and makes a parting motion in front of her chest.
“It is not really like this, is it...?”
Looking at her own gesture only makes her face turn paler.
“Why did I have to demonstrate it to myself?”
She is clearly frightened already.
After a moment, she suddenly looks down at her chest.
“It will be obvious when I wear a low neckline afterward, right...?”
“At a time like this...”
“I am still thinking about clothes.”

"It's scarier if you don't know. If you all explain it to me clearly, I'll feel at ease."
"So I really don't have to worry about anything?"
“Oh, are you standing as second assistant tomorrow?”
"Anyway, that's where it will be tomorrow. I'll finish it all today and I'll be familiar with it tomorrow."

“Here. Live version.”

"There's no problem with the movement. We'll arrange this tomorrow."

"I know you're totally up to it."

"You'd better be in such good spirits tomorrow."

Haruka’s voice softens.
“Then let’s talk about something else. Which team do you support?”
Haruka completes the epidural anesthesia confirmation.
“At least tell me what time it is now?”

Erina looks up at the surgical lights.
“Dr. Minato, I don’t believe the ‘very quickly’ you promised me today anymore.”

Erina glances down at the blanket over her legs.
“I was supposed to watch the baseball broadcast today.”

Erina is silent for a few seconds.
“...The Yomiuri Giants.”

Erina opens her eyes, half-asleep.
“...What time is it?”
“You’d better finish before two-thirty. I’m going back to my room, turning on the TV, and making sure I’m not still here when the game starts at three.”

Once the preparations are complete, Erina is covered with a blanket and seated on the transport stretcher. She glances at the time.
“...At least tell me what time it is.”
“The person I trust least today is you.”

“That schedule is wrong! I was only supposed to watch TV in my room today!”
She is finally fully awake, but the preoperative preparation has already begun.

“...Dr. Minato.”
Erina turns her head toward her.
“Do you know that today is Sunday?”

Erina looks at Sakaguchi.
“Who is he?”
“When you tell me not to worry, I worry even more.”
“Don’t act as if this was part of your plan!”

Erina lies back in bed, exhausted.
“...I made it.”

“The TV.”
She watches the screen, as if she has finally matched today’s schedule to the game time.
“At least I didn’t miss this one.”

Erina closes her eyes.
“...For the moment.”

Erina jolts fully awake.
“Today?! My surgery is tomorrow!”
“Thank you. At least there’s one person here who remembers the time.”

Erina looks at Haruka, then at Sakaguchi.
“...I don’t feel reassured at all.”
Erina is taken to the OR holding area. Haruka checks Sunday’s staffing arrangements and realizes that the original first assistant is nowhere in the hospital.

“Dr. Minato.”
Megumi’s eyes, visible above her mask, land precisely on Haruka.
“Focus on the surgery. Don’t hold a baseball discussion with the patient.”

“You’re welcome.”
She pauses.
“She’s always like this. Her hands are steady, and her mouth never stops.”
Megumi has already confirmed the instruments and sterile workflow inside the operating room, and passes the next thing to be done into Haruka’s hands.

Megumi does not argue about the date. She simply completes the preoperative preparations one by one: an enema, skin preparation, changing clothes, then gathering all of Erina’s hair beneath the surgical cap. Every step is professional and efficient.

Megumi looks down to confirm the schedule.
“It says today—Sunday, at ten twenty.”

“It’s seven-thirty in the morning. Good morning, Ms. Kinjo. Your surgery is at ten twenty today.”
Megumi has already placed the chart and preparation checklist beside the bed.
Sakaguchi takes the first-assistant position. Haruka takes the scalpel and makes a clean, precise incision in Erina’s abdomen.

“All right, Ms. Erina. We’re going to the operating room now.”
Megumi starts pushing the stretcher, preparing to leave the ward.
Megumi walks in. The preoperative supplies in her hands are arranged in order. Her movements are brisk, and her voice is steady.
“The Giants? Do you prefer watching pitching duels or batting battles?”

Haruka thinks for a moment.
“Don’t worry. You’ll make it. The surgery will finish on schedule.”

“See? You’ll definitely make it.”
Haruka does not look up; her hands remain steady.

Sakaguchi changes out of his scrubs and returns to the corridor, where he finds Haruka, also changed and holding her bag.

“Dr. Sakaguchi, do you have plans for the rest of today?”

The TV is already tuned to the game.
Sakaguchi finishes the last of his postoperative notes, leaving only the commentary from the game in the room.

“I am focusing.”
She does not stop working.
“Here—ease the retraction a little.”

Haruka Minato pushes open the door, her eyes settling on Erina, already seated on the transport stretcher.
“Good morning. Erina, are you ready?”

Haruka catches Sakaguchi as he happens to pass through the corridor.
“Dr. Sakaguchi, are you free today?”

Erina stares at Sakaguchi for two seconds.
“What? Is he reliable? Can he really operate? Or is he just some random person wandering around the hospital on a Sunday??”

Haruka comes in afterward.
“Did you get to watch it?”

“Don’t worry.”
Haruka keeps her eyes on the operative field.
“I’ll get you there in time.”

Haruka smiles.
“No problem. We promise everything will go smoothly!”

Haruka’s voice tightens.
“I know. Keep breathing steadily. I’ll handle this.”
She steps up to the operative field, and her voice settles into a more serious tone.

“Haruka Minato. I’m the lead surgeon today.”
She glances toward the operating room.
“As for you—I’ve just decided that you’re the first assistant.”
“Perfect. The patient is awake for an open procedure, and we’re short a first assistant. I’m borrowing you for the morning.”
“That’s exactly why I came to find you. A first assistant usually doesn’t just happen to be in the operating room on a Sunday.”

Haruka buys two cans of coffee from a vending machine and hands one to Sakaguchi.

“Thanks for saving the day.”

Haruka blinks and laughs as if nothing happened.
“Ahaha... The schedule’s been a little crowded lately. I accidentally squeezed Monday into Sunday.”

Sakaguchi is clearly not entirely convinced, but he does not press the question.

The two of them walk slowly along the riverside path through the city. Haruka is clearly in a good mood; she points out the trees along the bank, the water beneath the bridge, and the little shops on the corners, chatting enthusiastically with Sakaguchi about the neighborhood around the hospital.

Sakaguchi occasionally adds a comment, and before long they are talking easily together.

Haruka steps back with a bright smile.
“Then I’ll see you in the operating room.”

By the time they finish their coffee, the sky is beginning to darken. Haruka raises the empty can in her hand toward Sakaguchi.

“That’s enough for today. See you next time, Dr. Sakaguchi.”

She turns with a smile and walks away along the riverside path.

Haruka says with a bright smile:
“It’s such a nice day. Since you’re free too, Dr. Sakaguchi, shall we go for a walk together?”
“I may be a random person wandering around the hospital on a Sunday, but I know a little something about surgery.”
Sakaguchi looks at Haruka, then toward the operating room.
At two forty in the afternoon, Erina returns to her room. When the TV comes on, the baseball broadcast has not officially started yet.

Sakaguchi accepts the coffee and looks at her cautiously.
“You’re welcome. But... how did you manage to get the surgery date wrong?”

Sakaguchi looks at her.
“I did. Now... I don’t.”
The open cholecystectomy is completed successfully. Haruka makes the final checks, Megumi counts the instruments, and Sakaguchi assists with the handoff.

【Sunday Morning】
Erina Kinjo-Wang is still asleep.
