strings.collections.special_event_steps.probatio: “You could call it that.” Narumi answers without hesitation. “You will handle routine consultations yourself. I will not stand beside you and confirm every patient anymore.”
“When you truly cannot make sense of a case or are not sure, come find me.” “Independent practice does not mean forcing yourself to manage alone.”

“As of today, you are no longer listed as a probationary doctor.” Asuka taps the document. “You will handle routine outpatient consultations independently. The hospital also wants you to begin forming a regular working partnership of your own.”
After the director’s office door closes, Asuka slides a signed confirmation document to the center of the desk. Narumi stands by the window, while Ren holds the outpatient roster.
“I have not even asked anything yet.”

Ren turns the roster to the outpatient page. “I was already the one who usually joined Dr. Sakaguchi for preoperative explanations on the ward, or whenever you needed an extra pair of hands.” She rests a fingertip on the line bearing both their names. “But starting today, it will no longer be because I happened to be assigned. I am formally becoming Dr. Sakaguchi’s personal nurse.”
“That is why I said it in advance.” She hands Sakaguchi the outpatient roster. “I look forward to working with you, Doctor.”

“I will always be there for routine consultations. I can help confirm the order of tests and whether the evidence is sufficient.” “I will keep handling the ward’s preoperative explanations too. You can also call me when surgery needs a nurse, but you still choose each surgical team yourself.”
Ren closes the roster, then adds, “As for anything else—that is not allowed yet.”
strings.collections.special_event_steps.satsuki_:
Aqua is already walking away.
“Quickly.”
Satsuki hurries after her with the charts. “Chief, what do you mean by live—”

GYNECOLOGY NURSES’ STATION — DAY
Satsuki is sorting charts behind the counter when Aqua walks straight toward her.
“Oh. Dr. Sakaguchi will not affect the angle of the leg supports.”

“I called him. It’s new.”
Aqua pats the examination chair’s armrest.
“Because you are here. We are only testing positioning. No examination.”
Satsuki remains standing and glances unmistakably at Sakaguchi. Aqua follows her gaze and finally understands.
“The leg-support angle is not the problem!”

Satsuki stops for half a beat when she sees Sakaguchi.
“…D-Dr. Sakaguchi.”

Satsuki exhales slowly.
“…This is only a test, right? No surprise examination?”

GYNECOLOGY EXAM ROOM
A new electric examination chair stands in the center. Sakaguchi is reading its manual beside the controls.
“Aqua wants to see whether the team’s positions get in the way during actual use.”

Sakaguchi takes two steps back on his own.
“I will stand here. If that is still uncomfortable, I can leave.”

Satsuki looks from the chair to Aqua.
“So… who is the live subject?”

Sakaguchi merely greets her and does not approach. Satsuki adjusts her glasses.
“W-Why are you in gynecology…?”
Aqua lowers the support another notch.
Satsuki remains in uniform and wears her black-framed glasses. Her legs rest in the supports under a proper medical drape. Sakaguchi stays at a distance, watching the equipment and team positions.

Satsuki’s expression shifts from alarm to thought.
“…You did not tell me it was about to move.”

Aqua pauses and writes on her clipboard.
“Warn the patient before a position change.”
Satsuki removes her nursing shoes, straightens her uniform skirt, and sits on the chair. Aqua gives her a medical drape.

Aqua stops immediately.
“Did it pinch you?”
“I know. But when you are lying here… you do not know when it will move.”

Without warning, Aqua presses the control.
The motor whirs; the backrest lowers as the leg supports rise slightly.
“That is exactly why it is frightening.”

Satsuki lifts her head slightly.
“Chief, stand where you would during an examination.”

Aqua moves to the foot of the chair.
“Here?”
Aqua keeps writing. Sakaguchi lowers the manual and listens closely.
“Of course. This is where I stand for the examination.”
“When a nurse is standing, it feels as though the doctor is right beside the patient. Once you lie down, all you can see is the light.”

The chair reclines. Only the ceiling and examination light remain visible. Aqua is reduced to the edge of the frame, while Sakaguchi has stepped completely out of view. The supports and preparations cannot be seen.
“You hear footsteps, drawers, and instruments… but you do not know what anyone is about to do.”
“Or tell her directly that if anything is uncomfortable, we can readjust it now.”

“I’m fi—”
Satsuki stops, surprised by herself.
“…See? I almost said, ‘I’m fine.’”
“She may feel… that saying she is uncomfortable would inconvenience everyone.”
“Are the supports pressing anywhere? Is there a gap under the lower back? Are you cold?”
“It feels like only two when you are standing. It does not when you are lying down.”
“So we cannot simply ask, ‘Are you okay?’”
“Patients do this too. Especially once they are positioned and everyone is waiting.”
Aqua asks Sakaguchi to take the usual assistant’s position. He moves beside the equipment without approaching Satsuki.
“Right. It is better to ask something specific.”
Aqua stands at the foot and Sakaguchi at the side. The patient is quickly surrounded, and Satsuki visibly tenses.
“I told you to relax, so relax.”
Sakaguchi turns his face aside, suppressing a smile. Satsuki notices and blushes more deeply.

Her voice softens into her nursing tone.
“Next, the chair will recline a little farther and the leg supports will rise.”
“It may be a little uncomfortable. If it hurts or frightens you, tell me immediately.”
The room falls quiet. Aqua writes. Satsuki is still in an embarrassing position, but she no longer avoids Sakaguchi’s gaze.
Aqua returns to the examination position with an impeccably professional expression.
“You do not have to endure it. We can stop at any time.”

Satsuki thinks for several seconds before answering seriously.
“First, tell the patient what will happen next.”
“Once the patient knows what will happen next, many things become easier.”
“Fear, physical tension—even if she wants to refuse, she knows when she needs to speak.”
Satsuki looks at him. She is still nervous, but for the first time she does not want to retreat. Instead, she looks quietly, uncertainly pleased.

Satsuki seems to have expected to keep defending her point.
“…Just like that?”
“There is not enough time. Choose one.”
“If we could change only one thing?”
“Especially that an uncomfortable patient may not speak up. I will remember that.”
“What you just described is not something a doctor can see while standing.”
“Doctors easily focus only on whether the examination can be done. You notice what the patient is thinking. That is valuable.”

Satsuki blinks, then gives a small smile.
“…Okay.”

Satsuki looks down at herself, then at the chair.
“…Being a patient?”
The motor starts again. The backrest rises; Satsuki sits up and starts to remove her feet from the supports.
“Orikawa, you are very well suited to this.”

Satsuki slowly lowers her head.
“…Thank you.”
“Yes. The backrest is going to rise.”
Satsuki puts her nursing shoes back on. Alone with Sakaguchi, the only man in the room, she adjusts her glasses as some of her tension returns.

Aqua picks up the clipboard.
“I am going to ask Equipment Services to change a few settings.”
She walks straight out.
“Even if the doctors have already decided on the process?”

Sakaguchi does not approach.
“Nurse Orikawa, thank you for what you did just now.”
“No. You showed us what people standing beside the chair cannot see.”
“A process can listen to feedback. So can a patient.”

Satsuki takes a quiet breath.
“…Dr. Sakaguchi.”
“If you think something we do will make a patient more anxious, say so directly.”

This time, she does not stammer.
“Thank you for listening to me.”

HALLWAY
Satsuki walks back toward the nurses’ station alone. After a few steps, she stops and lightly adjusts her glasses.

A very small smile reaches Satsuki’s lips.
“He listens seriously.”

She remembers Sakaguchi’s words.
“You are right.”
“Keep speaking up.”

Satsuki Orikawa — Relationship Lv1
Clinical trust has been established. She has begun to believe that her patient-centered perspective deserves to be heard by the team.

GYNECOLOGY NURSES’ STATION — BEFORE THE END OF SHIFT
Satsuki stands at the edge of the counter, turning a rotation application over and over. Artoria walks past, then comes back.
“You have been staring at that paper for a long time.”

Satsuki adjusts her black-framed glasses.
“I am only deciding… whether I should really submit it.”
“I used to want very much to become an operating-room nurse.”
“Your eyes are different when you talk about Sugimura than when you talk about other nurses.”

Satsuki blushes.
“Senior Hiroko really is remarkable. When a patient is afraid, she knows when to speak.”
“When the doctors are busy, she knows when not to interrupt. She does not panic when something goes wrong.”
“I used to think… I wanted to become that kind of nurse too.”

Satsuki’s shoulders draw inward.
“Because… there were too many male doctors in surgery.”
“Do not accept that so calmly! It makes it sound even more embarrassing!”
“It is your reason. I have no right to be ashamed of it for you.”

Satsuki falls quiet.
“But lately I have been thinking… if every time I become nervous, I choose to avoid that place—”
“Then I will never know whether I could actually do the work well.”

She looks at the application.
“…Come with me once.”

NURSING ADMINISTRATION OFFICE
Ishigami sits behind her desk. Artoria is only accompanying Satsuki; she does not speak for her.
“You want to apply for a perioperative rotation.”

Her prepared answer catches in her throat.
“Because I want to become a better nurse.”
“That is an answer, not a reason.”
“…I used to want to work in surgery. Later, because of my own problem, I went into gynecology.”
“I like my work now. But I realized I never truly let go of that wish.”

Ishigami looks toward Artoria.
“Did you bring her here to vouch for her?”
“She asked me to accompany her. The application is hers.”
“You will begin with the basics: holding, patient transport, and preoperative handoff.”
“You will not take an instrument role yet.”
“Orikawa. Do not pretend you understand something because you are nervous.”
“Ask when you do not know. Say so when you cannot do something.”
“A problem affecting a patient matters far more than your embarrassment.”

SEVERAL DAYS LATER — OR HOLDING
Satsuki is here for the first time as a rotation nurse. She still wears her black-framed glasses and adjusts them more often than usual, but her work remains orderly.

First patient: identity check, transport, handoff—complete.
Second patient: just as smooth. No incident, only one real task completed after another.
The third patient is an adult woman, Yoriko Nikaido. Her hair is under a surgical cap, and her gown and sheet cover her body. She is trying hard to appear calmer than she feels.
“I will confirm once more. Please tell me your name.”

Satsuki completes the check. The patient speaks.
“Miss Nurse.”

Satsuki does not deny it reflexively.
“…A little.”

“You really said it.”
“I’m usually the one telling everyone else not to be nervous... It doesn’t seem to work very well today.”

The patient cannot help smiling.
“It is fine. Better than lying that you cannot tell at all.”

Satsuki relaxes a little too.
“I will take you inside. I will stay until the handoff is complete.”

OPERATING-ROOM CORRIDOR
Satsuki pushes the gurney along the corridor. Sakaguchi approaches from the changing area, headed for the same operating room.

The patient looks up at her.
“The surgeon?”

The patient studies her for two seconds, then lies back down.
“…I suddenly feel more nervous.”
“Why did seeing the doctor make you more nervous…?”
The automatic door opens. The room is brighter than the corridor; the patient sees the surgical lights, table, anesthesia machine, and waiting staff all at once.

Satsuki does not hear her clearly.
“What?”

The bed moves forward another little bit.
“Wait, wait—I heard that once you go in, everyone just focuses on prep and the patient can’t find a chance to say anything—is that true?!”

THUD.
The entire gurney stops abruptly.

Satsuki looks down at the wheels and tries a little more pressure. The gurney does not move at all.
“…?”
Satsuki immediately releases the pressure. Sakaguchi looks toward the front from the side.

SIDE VIEW OF THE DOORWAY
The patient has half sat up. Her legs spread to either side, each foot braced against one side of the entrance. The gurney is halfway through, but she has barred herself in place like a human door bolt.

Satsuki looks at the wheels, then at the patient.
“…The patient is stuck.”
The scene pauses for one beat. None of the staff laugh.
Satsuki instinctively reaches to pull the gurney back, then stops. She does not touch the patient’s legs. Instead, she moves to where the patient can see her directly.
“All right. We will not go in yet.”
Everyone behind them stops. No one continues pushing. The patient takes several breaths.
“I know I already consented. I know the operation is today.”
“Back in the ward, I still thought I was fine.”

She looks into the operating room.
“But when the door opened, when I saw that light, suddenly it felt—”

Her feet press harder against the frame.
“Like I was really being pushed inside.”

Satsuki is quiet for several seconds.
“Yes.”
“It means… I think what you feel is normal.”
“We see this doorway every day, so we forget what it looks like.”
“But today is the first time you have entered through it.”
“You do not have to put your feet down immediately.”
The patient visibly freezes in surprise.
“First, I will tell you what will happen after we enter.”
“After we enter, the gurney will first stop beside the operating table.”
“We will confirm your name, procedure, and wristband once more.”
“Only after that will we help you move onto the operating table.”
“Anesthesia will not suddenly begin the moment we enter, and no one will move you without explaining.”
“I will not leave before the handoff is complete.”
After several seconds, the patient slowly lowers her left foot from the frame. Satsuki still does not move the gurney.

The patient looks at the right foot still braced against the other side.
“...This foot is insurance. You always keep one line of defense.”
Sakaguchi turns his face slightly away. He is not mocking her; he is holding back a small smile.
“Then... when does the defense come down?”

One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
At last, the right foot slowly comes back inside.
Satsuki returns to the foot of the gurney and applies only the slightest pressure. It crosses the threshold. The patient does not brace her feet again.

OPERATING ROOM — FORMAL HANDOFF
The gurney stops beside the operating table. Hiroko receives them. Satsuki is still slightly tense when she begins, but her information is complete.
“Scheduled today for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. No known medication allergies. Preoperative preparation complete.”
“You stopped at the doorway for a while?”

The patient answers first.
“The gurney got stuck.”
Satsuki lowers her head. This time, she finally allows herself a small smile. Hiroko looks at her.

Satsuki glances at the patient.
“…The patient.”

The patient tucks her feet farther under the sheet.
“But I am inside now…”

Hiroko does not press the matter. She only smiles.
“Yes. What matters is that you came in.”

She looks back at Satsuki.
“Complete handoff. Good work.”

CORRIDOR OUTSIDE THE OR
The patient proceeds to the next stage of preparation. Satsuki stands outside looking as though she has just completed an operation herself. Sakaguchi comes out.
“But at first I thought a wheel was broken.”
“And then the patient was stuck in the doorway.”
Satsuki clearly imagines herself pushing desperately from behind while the patient braces desperately in front. Her expression changes.
“I actually… know what that feels like.”
“Your mind knows what you should do and everyone is waiting, but your body simply will not move.”

She adjusts her glasses.
“When that happened to me before, I only thought I was useless.”
“So when I saw her like that, I realized that if someone kept pushing, she would only become more afraid.”
“Then you are very well suited to this work.”
“Because you know when to continue, and when to stop first.”
Satsuki is still nervous and still blushes, but this time she does not immediately avoid his gaze.
“Dr. Sakaguchi. In the future… if I truly work in surgery…”
“I think I can work normally beside you.”
“Did you not already do that today?”

Satsuki stares for several seconds, then lowers her head with a smile.
“…I suppose I did.”
After Satsuki leaves, Hiroko steps out through the operating-room door.
“Her first formal rotation, and she encounters a patient like that.”

Hiroko looks at him.
“From whose perspective was that ‘good’?”

Hiroko smiles.
“Yes. She did one very important thing correctly.”
“No. She did not treat the patient as a joke.”
“Of course we find it funny. Anyone would want to laugh at two feet braced against a doorway.”
“But until the patient lowered her feet, Satsuki did not laugh.”
Hiroko returns to the operating room.

LATER THAT AFTERNOON — SCRUB AREA
After the rotation, Satsuki stays behind for a while. An unused pair of practice forceps rests on the training table.
The technique does. The expression does not.

When practice is over, she steps away from the sterile work area and lowers her mask to her chest. Seeing that Sakaguchi has not left, she holds up the practice forceps and puts on a very proud expression—one that lasts all of half a second.
“How do I look? Do I seem… a little more like an operating-room nurse now?”

“O-One more time?” She looks down at the practice forceps, then straightens in earnest.
“All right. But this time, you are not allowed to stand there and deliberately laugh at me.”

“Huh?” She touches her face without thinking, then realizes what he means.
“That is called composure. An excellent operating-room nurse can have a little composure too, can’t she?”

She blinks and quickly pulls her tongue back in, though she cannot suppress the smile at the corners of her mouth.
“O-Of course. I completed my first full rotation today, after all.”

Satsuki Orikawa — Relationship Lv2
She has proved that even while nervous, she can do her work beside Sakaguchi.

[Internal Medicine Ward - "What is the surgery? Can I eat it?"]
Yurika leaned against the bed. Next to the bed is a magazine that has been read many times. She turned a page. Pause for two seconds. Turn it back again.
A medical nurse passed by the door.
"The people in this hospital are becoming less and less service-oriented..."

There was the sound of wheels in the corridor. Satsuki appeared pushing the pre-operative preparation cart. She wears a white nurse uniform, black-rimmed glasses, and a surgical rotation name tag on her chest. Compared to Level 1, she no longer has the feeling of panicking as soon as she encounters a strange situation. Satsuki stopped beside the bed. Look down at the information.
Satsuki looks up. Seeing familiar patients.
"Ms. Orikawa. Is it your turn to torment me again today?"
"I recently had a gastroscopy, had blood drawn, and took strange medicines. Your hospital has too many projects, how do I know?"
"Of course you can't eat after surgery."
Satsuki couldn't help but smile. She opened the folder.
Yurika still maintained the relaxed expression just now.
Satsuki took a look at the information.
Satsuki just thought she was joking again.
"That's the disease you were admitted to the internal medicine department for."

Yurika’s expression changes to:

It turns out that the hospital discovered a new disease behind my back?
"How come you doctors can detect everything..."
Satsuki put on gloves and closed the bedside screen.
"Come over to your side. Bend your knees forward a little."
Yurika complied. When she saw the catheter prepared by Satsuki, her smile finally froze a little.
"It will cool down a little, and then it will swell. Don't shrink it suddenly."
"The more you explain, the more I want to shrink."
Satsuki held her hip steady with one hand.
When the catheter was inserted, Yurika's shoulders shrank suddenly.
"I told you it would be cold."
"I said and really Ryo are completely different things!"
"Don't pinch it. The more it pinches, the more uncomfortable it will be."
"It's my body that thinks this is suspicious!"
Satsuki began to pour in slowly. Yurika originally wanted to continue talking, but quickly frowned.
"I want to go to the toilet."
"No matter how gentle you scream, it's useless!"
Satsuki is finally over. Remove the catheter.
Yurika lay there and did not move immediately.
Yurika buried her face into the pillow.

[Skin Preparation - "Where is the incision?"]
Yurika became a little quieter after she came back. SatsukiRevisit the pre-operative checklist.
Yurika removes her patient gown as instructed and sits on the preparation chair. Satsuki places the skin-preparation supplies within reach.
“The hair over the lower abdomen and perineal area needs to be removed.”
Satsuki traces the approximate preparation area with a fingertip.
“This whole area, from the lower abdomen to the perineum.”
"…So we really have to cut from here?"
Satsuki spread the shaving cream. Cool foam adheres to the skin. Yurika inhaled sharply.
"Why do you say 'Don't move' every time?"
Satsuki picks up the disposable razor. Yurika blushed when she heard the small sound of the blade scraping her skin.
"Of course you can say that, because you're the one holding the razor."
Satsuki steadies the skin and works across the entire area from the outside inward. Yurika does not dare move and keeps staring at the ceiling.
"The skin here is thin. If you move around, I'll really scratch it."
SatsukiWipe off the foam. Check it over.
Yurika looks down at the freshly prepared area, then back up at Satsuki.
"So everyone who does surgery has to be like this?"
"I will do whatever I have to do."
"What if one day it's your turn?"
"I didn't know yesterday that it would be my turn today."
Satsuki was speechless for a moment.

[Changing - patient status completed]
Satsuki brought the covering sheet and surgical cap for surgical patients.
"Wear nothing. Cover this after you put on the stretcher."
"Because you insist on asking one by one!"
SatsukiPut the screen back together. Turn your back.
"Put the clothes on the chair. Call me when you're done."
There was the sound of fabric rubbing and buttons being unbuttoned from behind. After a while.
"Now I'm starting to regret asking so many questions."

Satsuki looks back. Yurika had taken off her hospital gown and underwear as required, and put a covering sheet in front of her. Clothes were neatly folded on the chair. She stepped onto the step stool with her bare feet and sat on the edge of the stretcher. Satsuki held her arms and asked her to lie flat. Put on the surgical cap and collect all the hair. Then pull the drape down from your shoulders to your ankles. Yurika looked down at herself.
"You just kept comforting me with 'Everyone is like this'."
"It doesn't sound more comforting at all."

Satsuki tidied up the edges of the list for her. Yurika was suddenly quiet. She looked at the flat covering sheet on her chest, the surgical cap, her exposed shoulders and arms, and then at the bare feet at the end of the bed.
"...It seems like we really need surgery."

[Transfer - "Why do I increasingly don’t know what I am doing"]
Corridor. The stretcher trolley moves forward. Yurika looked at the ceiling and stepped back.
"So what's going to happen in the end?"

CLATTER

Yurika is not fully awake yet. The abdomen has been bandaged. Satsuki stood beside the bed. Her face was paler than the patient on the bed. The nurse is recording vital signs.
Satsuki did not answer. Yurika frowned. Open your eyes slowly.

["I haven't forgiven you yet"]
Later. Yurika is fully awake. Satsuki is still there.

Small conference room. Ishigami, Hiroko, Satsuki, Sakaguchi were present. The complete accident record was placed in front of Shi Shen.

"I want to know what she really went through."

The room became quiet for a moment.

The stone god was silent. Hiroko didn't say anything either. Finally Sakaguchi spoke.

[Invite Yurika]
Yurika can now sit up and move around. Satsuki came to the ward again. Yurika frowned immediately when she saw her standing so formally.

Satsuki explained carefully. After listening to this, Yurika looked in disbelief.
"If you cut yours off, mine won't grow back."
"The head nurse Ishigami said the same thing."

"Not to make you forgive me."

"You don't have to forgive me just because I did it."
"Because I always thought I knew what it was like to be a patient."
"I realize now that I only know what it feels like to stand next to the bed."

Yurika laughed out loud. Satsuki blushes. Then take it seriously again:

Yurika looked at her for a long time.

[Morning of surgery day——Satsuki becomes a patient]
This time, Satsuki is not wearing a nurse uniform. She sits on the patient's bed. Still wearing black-rimmed glasses. Hiroko came in with a cart that was almost the same as that day. When Satsuki saw the car, her expression immediately stiffened. Hiroko stopped by the bed.
"You look a lot like Mito that day."

Satsuki slowly lay on her side. Bend your knees. Hiroko put on her gloves.
When the catheter entered, Satsuki's whole body visibly stiffened.

Pour in the medicinal solution. Satsuki holds the sheets.

Satsuki left her neatly folded patient gown and underwear on the chair, put on the surgical cap, and tucked all of her long hair inside it. She then lay barefoot on the stretcher. Hiroko covered her from the shoulders to the feet. Satsuki looked down at herself and said nothing for a long time.

[After surgery - "I know you didn't escape"]
Recovery room. Satsuki slowly wakes up. The regional anesthesia has not completely worn off. She still doesn't have glasses. The first reaction was to squint.

Satsuki is speechless. Yurika laughs. Laughed for a while. Be quiet.

Satsuki looked at the blurry figure. long time.

[Sakaguchi and Satsuki — “Come a Little Closer”]
Yurika left. Sakaguchi came to check Satsuki’s postoperative condition. He stood at his usual rounding distance, and Satsuki could see only a blurred outline.

strings.collections.staff.doc_aoi.name: Narumi Jinguji
strings.collections.staff.doc_aoi.personality: Mature and composed. She listens to the patient before looking at the numbers; gentle but opinionated, with occasional understated sarcasm.
“Assistant position confirmed. I’ll watch the field, but don’t forget what the patient told us.”
“We can continue for now. But listen to the patient’s response before deciding the next step.”
strings.collections.staff.doc_aqua.name: Aqua Mizuki
strings.collections.staff.doc_aqua.personality: A brilliant, enthusiastic, supremely confident, and somewhat scatterbrained young gynecology chief. She may trap herself in new equipment, but never compromises patient safety.
strings.collections.staff.doc_aqua.procedure_gro: “General surgery? I can help, but surely someone else is better suited... Fine. I’ll take it seriously.”
Aqua sets aside her disappointment with the procedure and rechecks the patient and plan to the standard expected of a department chief.
“Even outside gynecology, we still have to confirm these tissue planes. Continue.”
“Stop. The anatomy does not match the preoperative plan. Verify it again.”
“Assistant position confirmed. Even if it isn’t gynecology... fine. I’ll take it seriously.”
“Don’t rush. Hold the field and proceed according to the anatomy we already confirmed.”
Aqua confirms the patient, gynecologic procedure, and position. Her overexcited expression settles the instant the verification begins.
“Yes, right there. Excellent angle. Keep going. This field is beautiful... medically speaking!”
“Wait. The anatomy here is wrong. Stop and confirm the ureter’s position again.”
“Assistant position confirmed! I’ll watch the pelvic exposure and positioning. I like today’s procedure.”
“Don’t rush. Hold the field first. I’ve seen this before.”
strings.collections.staff.doc_aqua.team_dialogue: Aqua confirms the patient, procedure, and position. Her overexcited expression settles the instant the verification begins.
“Excellent angle. Keep going. This field is beautiful... medically speaking!”
“Wait. The anatomy here is wrong. Stop and confirm the ureter’s position again.”
“Assistant position confirmed. I’ll watch the pelvic exposure and positioning.”

strings.collections.staff.doc_artoria.name: Artoria Pendragon
strings.collections.staff.doc_artoria.personalit: A rigorously disciplined, fair, and steadfast knightly leader. She puts everyone where they can contribute best and accepts final responsibility herself.
strings.collections.staff.doc_artoria.team_dialo: Artoria confirms everyone’s role and the contingency plan, then nods her acceptance.
Artoria repeats the personnel, instruments, and backup plan item by item, confirming that nothing is missing.
Artoria assists with the field while maintaining the team’s rhythm with the briefest possible instructions.
Artoria does not raise her voice. She simply identifies the most urgent adjustment: “Correct this first. Everyone else, hold.”
“I will take the assistant position. You will make the final judgment; leave the team’s rhythm to me.”
“Everyone remain at your posts. Dr. Sakaguchi, continue managing the field. Leave everything outside it to me.”
strings.collections.staff.doc_asuka.name: Asuka Shiromiya
strings.collections.staff.doc_asuka.personality: Warm, intelligent, inquisitive, and steadfast. She speaks gently, but her formal decisions leave no room for ambiguity.
strings.collections.staff.doc_asuka.team_dialogu: Asuka Jomiya carefully reviews the operative plan and quietly confirms that she will hold the assistant position.
Asuka Jomiya knows the operating-room workflow intimately. Her replies are concise, and her coordination leaves almost no unnecessary pause.
strings.collections.staff.doc_emiko.name: Emiko Mido
strings.collections.staff.doc_emiko.personality: Aloof, confident, and forceful in her judgment, with a habit of taking control. Once she truly loves someone, she is exceptionally devoted.
strings.collections.staff.doc_emiko.team_dialogu: Emiko Mido scans the preoperative information and calmly says that she has the key points.
Emiko Mido accepts the task with a short, precise instruction and moves without the slightest hesitation.
strings.collections.staff.doc_minato.team_dialog: Haruka Minato reviews the preoperative information, confirms the patient and procedure, and naturally sets aside the scheduling problem she created for herself.
Haruka Minato confirms the patient, the procedure, and every team member's role. She may forget the date, but she never forgets who she is caring for.
At the operative field, Haruka Minato quickly sheds her relaxed tone, confirms the patient's condition from memory, and gives a steady, precise judgment.
"Lead surgeon confirmed. I have checked the patient and the procedure. Let's begin."
"Don't rush. Hold the field. I'll confirm the next step."
strings.collections.staff.doc_rei.name: Kaori Miyama
strings.collections.staff.doc_rei.personality: Direct and decisive in her clinical judgment.
strings.collections.staff.doc_sakura_anesthesiol: Calm, strict, and direct; she never treats anesthesia as a menu for the surgeon.
“I am responsible for the anesthetic plan. If I need surgery to pause, I will say so directly.”
“The general anesthetic plan, monitoring, and backup access are confirmed.”
“The circulatory change remains within a controllable range. Continue, but keep this pace.”
“Hands off. Wait until circulation is stable again before continuing any irreversible step.”
“Anesthesia position confirmed. From induction onward, the patient is mine.”
strings.collections.staff.doc_sayaka.name: Sayaka Nanjo
strings.collections.staff.doc_sayaka.personality: Mature, cheerful, and highly adaptable. She knows when she is flirting and when to stop, and never mistakes a light touch for irresponsibility.
strings.collections.staff.doc_sayaka.team_dialog: “Assistant? Sure. But for something difficult, you should find a specialist. I can handle ordinary cases.”
Sayaka Nanjo reviews the procedure and role requirements, confirms that they do not exceed her limits, then smiles and writes her name in the assistant slot.
“The field is stable. You look rather handsome giving orders like that—don’t stop your hands. Continue.”
“Understood. I’ll follow your judgment here, step back, and verify it again.”
“Assistant position confirmed. Tell me if you need me to fill in, and I’ll also tell you directly if something exceeds my ability.”
“Separate the vital signs from the surgical field. Deal with what we can one item at a time; don’t panic about everything at once.”
strings.collections.staff.doc_shiori.name: Shiori Fujisaki
strings.collections.staff.doc_shiori.personality: A gentle, poised, disciplined, and versatile young internist. She assembles scattered facts into a complete picture of the patient, while hiding a fierce competitive streak and exacting standards.
strings.collections.staff.doc_shiori.team_dialog: “I can assist, but to be clear, I’m not a surgeon. I’ll be more useful watching the patient’s overall condition than the field. (I’m a little nervous... but I should be able to do this.)”
Shiori Fujisaki rechecks the patient’s cardiopulmonary status, metabolism, and long-term medications before signing the team list.
“Circulation is stable for now. You can continue, but do not focus only on what is directly in front of you.”
“Understood. I judged too quickly. Continue; I’ll verify it again.”
“Assistant position confirmed. But if the patient’s perioperative condition changes, I’ll say so immediately. I won’t wait for you to ask.”
“Don’t panic. Leave the surgical problem to the surgeon. I’ll reassess the other vital signs.”

“Some of the findings do fit, but what about the rest? I'm worried we might have missed something.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_rin.personal_nur: “Dr. Sakaguchi, something about this diagnosis concerns me. That result we just reviewed seems to argue against it.”
“Mm, it does explain some of the findings. But we still have these other results to account for, so let's not settle on it just yet.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_yui.personal_nur: “Oh, Doctor, that doesn't match the test results. Aren't you jumping to conclusions a little quickly today?”
“You've explained the findings that fit. What about the ones that don't? We can't just pretend they aren't there.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_ange.personal_nu: “Dr. Sakaguchi, please check again. This diagnosis contradicts the current test evidence and cannot be accepted as it stands.”
“It explains only some of the findings. The other abnormalities still lack a reasonable explanation. I believe it is too early to draw a conclusion.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_hiroko.personal_: “Mr. Sakaguchi, there's no need to rush. This result doesn't match the diagnosis you just gave. Let's check it once more.”
“There are still several other findings we can't explain. Let's work through the test results together before we decide.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_moe.personal_nur: “Huh? Dr. Sakaguchi… Doesn't this test result differ from what we'd expect with that diagnosis? Oh, did I read it wrong?”
“Th-these findings make sense to me… But what about the rest? Can we really be sure?”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_satsuki.personal: “M-Mr. Sakaguchi… I've checked the test records, and this diagnosis seems inconsistent with one of the findings. Could we check it again?”
“U-um… It explains some of the findings, but there are several others we still can't account for. I think… it might be too early to draw a conclusion.”

strings.collections.staff.nurse_haru.personality: Perceptive and pragmatic, with a strong respect for ordinary life. Usually reserved, but unwavering where patient safety is concerned.
strings.collections.staff.nurse_haru.preop_graph: “Just do not frighten yourself so badly that your legs give way. We still have to prepare you.”
“Am I being too specific? If I leave it out now, you may imagine something worse on the operating table.”
“Do not be afraid. It sounds frightening, but everyone knows exactly what to do.”
“Tell me to stop if you have heard enough. But since you asked, I am going to answer you properly.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_haru.team_dialog: “I can circulate or scrub. If anything in the handoff is unclear, I’ll ask on the spot.”
“The patient said we may continue, not that nothing is wrong. Judge her by what she actually said.”

strings.collections.staff.nurse_hiroko.personali: Gentle and approachable, with quiet inner strength—the dependable big-sister nurse who takes care of everyone.
strings.collections.staff.nurse_hiroko.preop_gra: “That is the general outline. If you think of anything else that worries you, press the call button and ask for me.”
“This part sounds a little frightening, does it not? It is all right. When it happens, I will be beside you and guide you one step at a time.”
“You do not need to pretend to be brave. Pain, cold, fear—you may say any of them out loud.”
“Of course. I will explain it slowly. If hearing it becomes uncomfortable, tell me; we can pause.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_ishigami.name: Chizuru Ishigami
strings.collections.staff.nurse_ishigami.persona: A cool, taciturn and highly observant Head of Nursing. She almost never raises her voice, yet can restore order across the nursing service with a few calm words.
strings.collections.staff.nurse_ishigami.special: Hospital-Wide Nursing Management / Nursing Safety & Resource Coordination
strings.collections.staff.nurse_ishigami.team_di: “I will not occupy an ordinary position. I’ll watch nursing staffing, rotations, and supplies. You keep doing the surgeon’s job.”
Ishigami checks nursing coverage, rotation times, and backup supplies item by item, confirming that no position depends on someone simply enduring exhaustion.
“The nursing side is stable. Continue, but do not focus only on what is directly in front of you.”
“Handle it first. Cause and responsibility can wait until the patient is safe.”
“Nursing supervision confirmed. I will not make medical judgments for you, and I will not allow the nursing side to run on overwork.”
“Who is treating the patient, who is calling support, and who is documenting? Say it clearly, then continue.”

strings.collections.staff.nurse_moe.personality: Earnest and endearingly absentminded, with severe myopia. The harder she tries to do everything right, the more likely she is to stumble somewhere unexpected.

strings.collections.staff.nurse_rin.personality: Mature, easygoing, reliable, and restrained. She readily sees through what patients conceal, yet rarely discusses her own past.
strings.collections.staff.nurse_rin.preop_graphi: “It is good that you asked. The hardest patients are the ones who nod the whole way, then admit at the door that they understood none of it.”
“You said you were not afraid, but you have been gripping that blanket the entire time. I will explain this part more slowly.”
“Something sounding frightening is not the same as something going wrong. If we need to stop, we will know before you do.”
“You really want to hear it? All right. Let us clear up the easiest parts to misunderstand before you are lying there pretending everything is fine.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_rin.team_dialogu: “I’ll verify the ward handoff and transport documents. Dr. Sakaguchi, just make sure the first time you see the whole patient isn’t after she is already on the table.”
“Handoff, identity, position, and warming are confirmed. Surgery does not begin with the incision.”
“Everything on this side of the table is stable. The vital signs and lines are visible. Go ahead.”
“Understood. I judged that step by an old habit, and I’ve corrected it. Keep going; I’ll complete the record.”
“Circulating position confirmed. I’ll handle equipment, records, and movement outside the sterile field. If information breaks down at any step, I’ll stop the room.”
“One thing at a time. Who is treating the patient, who is calling for help, and who is documenting what happened? Don’t let everyone do the same job at once.”
strings.collections.staff.nurse_satsuki.name: Satsuki Orikawa
strings.collections.staff.nurse_satsuki.personal: A serious, courteous, bookish young nurse. She becomes visibly nervous around men, yet notices subtle details in how patients experience care.
strings.collections.staff.nurse_satsuki.preop_gr: “Those are the main points. I am sorry for being so detailed... but before you go in, I want you to know how you can speak up.”
“A textbook often reduces this part to one term, but a patient actually experiences it as several different sensations.”
“If any sensation goes beyond what I just described, tell us immediately. You do not have to endure it merely to cooperate.”
“Yes. I will explain it in the order you are likely to feel it, instead of giving you only the names of the steps.”

strings.collections.staff.nurse_yui.personality: Cheerful and conscientious, diligent about confirming procedures in a new environment. Professionally humble and steady in practice.

“The procedure is fine. I’m checking Hoshimi’s documentation order, not the basic steps.”

strings.collections.staff.pharmacist_manami.pers: Gentle, cautious, and strongly guided by justice.
strings.collections.staff.pharmacist_manami.team:
“I-I have almost no experience in the surgical field... Since you insist, I’ll do only what you explicitly assign. Please correct me whenever necessary.”
(I only dispense medication, and they really put me on the surgical team. Don’t panic. At least I understand the drugs and doses.)

“Team assignment... understood. I’ll review the steps again beforehand.”
(It is too late to back out now. At least I must not make everyone spend extra attention on me.)

“I completed this step as instructed, but I cannot judge whether it is enough. Please confirm it.”
(I can barely match the tissue on the screen to its name. Stay calm and describe exactly what I see.)

“Wait, that last step seems different from the preoperative plan... Did I remember it incorrectly?”
(I can barely match the names to the structures, but this really is different. Better to ask and be wrong than remain silent.)

“Assistant position confirmed. Tell me every step directly, and I’ll ask immediately if I’m unsure.”
(An assistant surgeon? I am a pharmacist... First, review the procedure name and the anatomy again.)

“I’m holding the position you indicated, but is this angle correct? Please check again.”
(What structure is this...? I have barely seen it since anatomy class, and I have forgotten almost everything. Do not pretend to know. Ask the surgeon.)
strings.collections.staff.visiting_futaba.name: Futaba Sakura
strings.collections.staff.visiting_futaba.person: A brilliant, curious, direct, and slightly eccentric adult physician-scientist. More mature and socially capable now, she retains her geeky humor, leaps of thought, and extreme focus while learning to live with past trauma and guilt.
strings.collections.staff.visiting_futaba.proced: “I can assist. You decide where the blade goes; I’ll watch why she changes at that particular moment.”
“The change is not random. Her breathing and heart rate rose together only after she heard the explanation of the next step.”
“Understood. I’ll defer to the facts in the field and test my explanation again.”
“Assistant position confirmed. Fear, Pain, and Cooperation are more than numbers. I’ll watch why they change.”
“Let Maya verify the signal first. If it is real, I’ll trace its timing against the psychological stimulus.”
strings.collections.staff.visiting_futaba.specia: Visiting Physician-Scientist / Mind–Body Interaction & Psychodynamic Research
strings.collections.staff.visiting_futaba.team_d: “I can assist. Do not expect much independent surgical judgment, but I’ll watch the patient’s fear, pain expectations, and changes in cooperation.”
Futaba quickly reviews the patient’s fear, pain, and cooperation records, confirms that she will provide only limited assistance and psychophysiologic observation, then signs the assistant slot.
“The heart-rate change is real, but the timing is wrong. She became anxious after hearing ‘the next step.’ This is not entirely pain.”
“Understood. I became too attached to explaining the cause. I’ll reset the field maneuver according to your judgment.”
“Assistant position confirmed. The brain is an organ too. Stop pretending it does not take part in surgery.”
“Do not interpret every number as injury. Ask what she just heard, then see exactly when the change began.”
strings.collections.staff.visiting_maya.name: Maya Ibuki
strings.collections.staff.visiting_maya.personal: An earnest, humble, dependable, and slightly reserved adult physician-researcher. She prizes data and equipment reliability, while strong emotions often show first in her eyes.
strings.collections.staff.visiting_maya.procedur: “Abdominal surgery... I can handle monitoring and equipment. Give me explicit instructions for any work in the field.”
“The vital signs are stable. The abdominal images remind me of some old work, but that will not affect my judgment.”
“Understood. I mixed old experience into this operation. I’ll verify it again according to the clinical steps.”
strings.collections.staff.visiting_maya.specialt: Visiting Physician-Researcher / Biomedical Engineering, Medical Devices & Physiological Monitoring
strings.collections.staff.visiting_maya.team_dia: “I am not a surgeon, but you can leave monitoring, equipment, and physiologic signals to me. If you need me to work in the field, state the scope and purpose clearly.”

“The raw waveform matches the patient’s condition. The equipment is reliable for now. I’ll assist in the field as instructed.”
“Understood. I let my equipment assessment influence the field too quickly. I’ll confirm the position again.”
“Special assistant position confirmed. I’ll watch the machines, and I’ll warn you when they may be lying.”
“Compare the patient, raw waveform, and backup monitor first. Do not let one abnormal trace make the decision for us.”

strings.collections.temporary_conditions.drowsin: Ask the assistant surgeon to keep calling to her and repeat instructions
“Look at me and stay awake. I will tell you, one sentence at a time, how far we have progressed.”
Ask the circulating nurse to continue observation and verbal stimulation
“I will keep watching her responses. Listen to my voice and slowly tell me your name and where you are.”
Continue the operation without interrupting the current task
The patient’s gaze drifts again, and she gives no answer to the last instruction.
Call to her personally and reassess consciousness and command following
“I can hear you... please keep telling me what comes next.”
“Doctor... my eyelids feel so heavy... I'm still awake, but I can hardly keep my eyes open...”
“...What did you just say? I'm sorry, I keep losing track of your voices...”
“I... can't hear clearly anymore... Don't let me drift off... Please, please keep calling to me...”
Ask the assistant surgeon to stabilize the patient and explain the situation
“I will maintain her position and explain what is happening. Slow your breathing; we will settle the nausea first.”
Ask the circulating nurse to prepare suction and a cool towel and reassure her
“Suction and a cool towel are ready. I am right here—breathe slowly, and do not force yourself to speak.”
Maintain the current pace and do not intervene yet
“Ugh... the nausea has not stopped... I cannot hold it much longer...”
Pause, reassure her personally, and adjust her position
“...That is better. Thank you for stopping first.”
“Doctor... I feel a little sick... My stomach keeps churning...”
“Ugh... I feel awful... I, I'm about to throw up. I can't control my body...”
“No... I'm really going to be sick... Please stop for a moment. I can't take it anymore...!”
strings.collections.time_events.clinic_chat_doc_: She mentions an easily missed detail from today’s clinic. They do not dissect the case, merely exchange a few thoughts.

Sayaka folds a complicated health-management chart into three columns and smiles. “Things we can handle, things that need consultation, and things we do not need to frighten ourselves about today. People work the same way.”
After hearing Sakaguchi’s assessment, Sayaka does not immediately agree. She gently points to a long-term medication he missed. “You look at the lesion. I’ll help you see the whole person.”
Sayaka takes the temporary consultation form. “I can cover ordinary difficulty. If it needs a genius, you will have to call an actual genius.”
strings.collections.time_events.clinic_chat_nurs: With the clinic briefly quiet, Hiroko and Sakaguchi exchange a few observations about the emotions of patients in the waiting room.
After arranging the examination-room supplies, Hiroko warns Sakaguchi that the next patient may be more anxious than the chart suggests.
She smiles and says that the ward and clinic move at completely different rhythms, but both begin by making the patient feel heard.
Moe carefully finishes checking the clinic record. Only when she looks up does she notice her glasses have slipped down her nose; she hurriedly adjusts them before continuing her report.
She pulls a small notebook covered in arrows from her pocket and solemnly announces that she has recorded every route in the hospital where one is most likely to get lost.
Worried that she missed a detail, Moe checks the same preparation twice. When she notices, she blushes and says that checking once too often is better than once too little.
She quietly tells him about a small incident in the clinic, then starts laughing halfway through her own story.
strings.collections.time_events.exam_chat_doc_re: She complains that the machine lagged by half a beat again, then asks whether Sakaguchi is adjusting. The conversation is brief, but feels more natural than silence.
strings.collections.time_events.imaging_chat_vis: Discuss Psychophysiological Data with Futaba Sakura

Futaba overlays the waveforms from before and after the patient heard the word ‘incision.’ “See? The signal is clean. The patient is not anxious for no reason. Her body is simply answering before her mouth does.”

Staring at a set of recovery data, she suddenly says, “Beautiful.” When she notices Sakaguchi looking, she adds, “I know the patient is still here. The data are beautiful precisely because they are hers.”

Futaba places Maya’s calibration report on the left and the interview notes on the right. “The machine proves the change is real; language tells us why it happened. Put them together and you have the complete case.”
Review Monitoring Data with Maya Ibuki

Maya enlarges two nearly overlapping waveforms. “The difference is small, but enough to show that this probe needs recalibration. Machines bear no malice. They only repeat an error with perfect diligence.”

She looks first at the bedside record, then at the equipment log. “Dr. Sakaguchi sees the patient. I see how the machine sees the patient. When those disagree, neither of us should rush to a conclusion.”
Maya closes the equipment report and adds softly, “I checked three times. It is not that I distrust you... the third check simply makes me feel safer.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Narumi Jinguji
Narumi Jinguji asks over tea whether Sakaguchi has settled in, then shares a small trick she uses to keep her shifts organized.
Their conversation moves from today’s cases to the cafeteria’s new menu. Narumi listens closely, adding an occasional gentle comment.
Narumi gives Sakaguchi the seat by the window and reminds him not to forget to drink water when work gets busy.
Chat with Kaori Miyama
Kaori Miyama asks whether Sakaguchi is satisfied with several of today’s decisions, then seriously reviews them with him.
The subject turns to time off. Kaori says she does not care, though she has already listed three places she wants to visit.
Kaori remarks that Sakaguchi’s movements were sharper than yesterday, then lowers her eyes to her coffee.
Chat with Sayaka Nanjo
Sayaka sits opposite him with her coffee. “You may understand this as a break, or as me deliberately arranging a chance encounter.”
She talks about her two years in a school infirmary, where she learned that the same words—‘my stomach hurts’—could conceal ten entirely different problems.
Sakaguchi asks why she appears in so many departments. Sayaka laughs. “Because I do not have one place where I am the best. Put another way, I can help a little almost anywhere.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_nurs: Chat with Ren Nanase
Ren Nanase asks whether Sakaguchi has eaten properly, then shares a small but reassuring change she noticed in a patient today.
They talk about the ward. Ren speaks gently, but remembers every patient’s details with remarkable clarity.
Ren hands him a cup of warm water and smiles, saying that rest is part of the job too.
Chat with Mika Nakai
Mika Nakai and Sakaguchi review the priorities for the next handoff. Only after the work is settled do they discuss a recent movie.
They talk about teamwork. Mika points out a small unspoken habit Sakaguchi had missed, then naturally asks which night-shift food he disliked most overseas.

Mika pushes the last snack toward Sakaguchi and says everyone worked hard today. When someone suggests a weekend group photo, she smiles and agrees, asking only to stand at the edge in case a call comes in.

The news mentions a cold case unsolved for years. Watching the screen, Mika says, “As long as someone works normally, pays taxes on time, and remembers to greet the neighbors, most people never investigate her twice.” Then she offers Sakaguchi the remote. “Change the channel?”
Chat with Miyuki Asakura
Miyuki Asakura lays out handoff forms from two hospitals. Once she learns Hoshimi’s local rules, she quickly summarizes the differences.
Miyuki recounts taking the wrong corridor when she first arrived at Hoshimi, laughing that knowing nursing does not mean knowing every building.
They spend half an hour on her orientation checklist. She crosses off everything she has mastered, leaving only the hospital-specific customs she still needs to confirm.
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_visi: Get Something to Eat with Futaba Sakura
Futaba answers an email while unwrapping curry bread. Sakaguchi glimpses only the words ‘Dr. Maruki’ before she snaps the laptop shut. “Research discussion. No Easter egg.”
She curls into the corner of the sofa with her drink, far more casually than she ever sits in her lab coat. “Successful socialization does not require sitting like a textbook illustration.”

Futaba suddenly asks, “If you believed the wrong cause for years, even though it was wrong, does learning the truth count as healing?” Before he can answer, she bites into her bread. “Never mind. Sample size one. No conclusion possible.”
Take a Break with Maya Ibuki
Beside her healthy lunch, Sakaguchi finds a packet of cat-shaped cookies. Maya adjusts her glasses. “They provide quick sugar during experiments. Their shape... has nothing to do with the research.”
Sakaguchi notices the cat-shaped cushion at her temporary workstation. Maya is silent for two seconds. “It did not come from NERV. It is new.”
Someone says she has been looking increasingly like a certain Dr. Akagi. Maya immediately lowers her head to organize her papers. “N-no, I have not... This is simply practical clothing.”

strings.collections.time_events.or_chat_nurse_an: While checking the instrument list, Ange asks how Sakaguchi usually gives orders when plans change unexpectedly. After listening, she seriously points out two places where his wording could cause confusion.
The topic moves from operating-room scheduling to the emergency department. Ange complains that whenever she says she will help for only a moment, she always ends up too busy to eat.
Ange asks how preparations for Sakaguchi’s next operation are going. Satisfied with his answer, she nods and insists she is merely checking normally and is absolutely not especially excited.
strings.collections.time_events.or_chat_nurse_ha: As she organizes the count sheet, she describes a small operating-room habit that newcomers often overlook.
strings.collections.time_events.or_chat_nurse_mo: Moe puts on her glasses and checks the room sign repeatedly before entering the surgical area. When she notices Sakaguchi watching, she blushes and explains that she is simply following her anti-getting-lost procedure.
Holding her little notebook, she reviews the surgical hand-scrub steps one by one with such concentration that she nearly starts again from the beginning.
Moe quietly says that she is still unfamiliar with the operating room and asks Sakaguchi to tell her immediately if he sees a problem. Then she nods as forcefully as if accepting a medical order.
strings.collections.time_events.pharmacy_chat_ma: She closes the register and mentions that people have recently been confusing medications with similar packaging.
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Talk with Narumi Jinguji
Looking into the distance, Narumi says that difficult things seem a little less pressing from higher up.
She asks which patient is weighing most heavily on Sakaguchi today. Together, they slowly put that worry into words.
Narumi does not hurry to discuss work. She simply watches the clouds with Sakaguchi for a while.
Talk with Kaori Miyama
Kaori says she only came up for air, yet casually points out one judgment Sakaguchi could improve from today.
For once, she does not hurry him along. She only asks whether he wants to stay until the wind dies down.
Watching the ambulance entrance, Kaori candidly admits that some decisions make her nervous too.
Spend Some Time in the Wind with Sayaka Nanjo
Sayaka leans against a spot one step back from the railing. “Relax, I only came up for air. If I wanted to create a scene where you had to rescue me, I would choose a safer method.”

Looking toward the distant school roof, she speaks of her time as a school health teacher. “Those two years were not a detour. They only made me more certain that I want to be someone who can keep following a problem.”
The wind blows her red hair across her shoulder. Holding down the ends, she tilts her head. “Are you this good at listening on Sundays too, Dr. Sakaguchi?”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_nur: Talk with Ren Nanase
Ren says the rooftop is a good place to set down the feelings she had no time to sort out on the ward.
She asks whether Sakaguchi is tired. The simple question finally loosens shoulders that have been tense all morning.
Ren points to the light between the clouds and says the patient discharged today can probably see it too.
Talk with Mika Nakai
Standing beside Sakaguchi, Mika talks about each team member’s inconspicuous but important habits.
She says a smooth handoff is like the wind: invisible, but immediately noticeable when it is gone.
Mika slows her speech for once and discusses where to go on their next day off. When Sakaguchi asks where she used to go, she smiles. “Are you asking me out, or conducting a background check?”

The staff entrance below is getting a new access system. Mika casually identifies which elevator still reaches the wards at night, pauses, and adds, “Work enough night shifts and you remember these things.”
Talk with Miyuki Asakura
Miyuki meant to bring her workflow notes upstairs, but ends up spending half an hour discussing favorite desserts with Sakaguchi.
She points out a train in the distance, then casually confirms tomorrow’s handoff location for cross-department support.
Miyuki says she now recognizes every clinical area. The one route she still gets wrong leads to the staff cafeteria.
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_pause.la: Spend Some Time in the Wind
strings.collections.time_events.station_chat_nur: She pushes the handoff sheet aside and talks with Sakaguchi about the ward’s rhythm today.

A photo of an old drug package is tucked into the training material. Mika casually names the color change from before and after it was discontinued. When asked, she only says, “I heard about it at an old job,” and continues checking the next page.

Sakaguchi asks which hospital she worked at before. Stamping a form, she answers, “A few.” Asked why she left, she smiles. “The work environment did not suit me. Is the next question my family history?”
During a break in the paperwork, she asks whether Sakaguchi has learned his way around the entire hospital yet.
strings.collections.time_events.ward_chat_nurse_: While checking the ward record, Hiroko talks with Sakaguchi about the small changes that are easiest to miss during recovery.
She gathers the scattered forms for a busy junior, then turns and gently asks whether Sakaguchi has eaten properly today.
The subject moves from the ward handoff to Manami Iimura’s latest complaint about medication stock. As Hiroko talks, her smile grows helpless but affectionate.
She tells him about a patient on the ward who finally slept soundly. They talk a little longer before the handoff bell rings.
A patient insists that she “doesn’t hurt much.” Mika raises the observation level. “She looked at the door three times when she said ‘really.’ Ask again after her family leaves.”
strings.collections.ward_preparation_cg_pools.wa: Following the ward preparation protocol, Dr. Sakaguchi personally completes the enema.
She struggles to hold the position while Dr. Sakaguchi completes the lower-abdominal and perineal skin preparation.

strings.collections.ward_preparation_cg_pools.tr: The ward nurse takes over the stretcher and brings the patient to the operating room with her IV line and warming blanket in place.
Ward Preparation · Transport to the Operating Room
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_advice.text: I've read your résumé, Dr. Sakaguchi. But a résumé only says what you have done before. Starting today, we'll see how you judge a situation and how you speak in front of a patient. If you're unsure, ask. You don't need to force yourself to look like a seasoned doctor.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_composed.text: Good. The pace here can accelerate without warning, though. Keep up when you can, and speak up when you cannot. Saying something in time is also part of a doctor's judgment.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_first_impression.text: The person assigned to meet Ryuji Sakaguchi is already waiting by the window. She holds a chart against her chest, her white coat immaculate. When she sees him, her gaze first settles on his name badge, and only then does a faint smile appear. It is less a rehearsed welcome than the manner of a senior doctor accustomed to observing before she speaks.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_honest.text: It's normal to be nervous. The real danger is being too tense to hear anyone else while pretending you know everything. Just stay as you are now.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_question.choices.1.la: I'll get up to speed as quickly as I can.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_question.text: Your first day in an unfamiliar hospital—are you nervous?
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_welcome.text: Good morning. Dr. Sakaguchi, correct? I'm Narumi Jinguji from General Surgery. I'll show you around today.
strings.dialogue.nodes.arrival.text: April sunlight streams through the glass corridor of Hoshimi Hospital. After completing his training overseas, Ryuji Sakaguchi had not planned to choose his next post immediately. With his record, he had more prominent options.
strings.dialogue.nodes.clinic_handover.text: This is your examination room, Dr. Sakaguchi. The first patient has arrived, and I'll be nearby to assist. When you're ready, we can begin.
strings.dialogue.nodes.clinic_walk.text: Ren Nanase opens the door at the end of the corridor. Charts, a stethoscope, and newly delivered test forms are arranged neatly on the desk. Beyond the door comes the muted conversation of waiting patients. Only now does the reality of a first day about to begin truly settle in.
strings.dialogue.nodes.first_day.text: The scent of disinfectant is faint. A cart rattles past the corner. The new name badge in his white-coat pocket rests against his chest. Today is Ryuji Sakaguchi's first day here.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_arrival.text: As she finishes speaking, light but measured footsteps approach from the other end of the corridor. A nurse carrying neatly arranged outpatient files stops before them, nods first to Dr. Jinguji, then turns to Sakaguchi.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_first_impression.tex: She keeps her eyes on Sakaguchi as she speaks. Her voice is gentle, but the movement with which she hands him the files is crisp and efficient. Colored tabs line the pages, and even the ward and operating-room locations he has not yet asked about are marked with brief notes.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_intro.text: It's nice to meet you. I'm Ren Nanase. I mainly handle surgical nursing and today's coordination. Your outpatient files are ready. If you cannot find someone later, come to the nurses' station first. You can usually find me there.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_invite.text: We have a little time before the first patient's appointment. Let's stop by the nurses' station and meet today's team. Then I'll take you to the examination room.
strings.dialogue.nodes.mentor_recommendation.tex:
What finally brought him to Hoshimi Hospital was a recommendation from his medical-school mentor.
“If you still haven't decided where to go, give this place a try.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.one_year_contract.text: Sakaguchi ultimately signed a one-year contract. For now, Hoshimi was simply a place to settle after returning to Japan.
strings.dialogue.nodes.rin_impression.text: Nurse Nakai turns to the next page of her handoff sheet. Her tone is almost stern in its brevity, yet she has already written an extension number beside Sakaguchi's name. She seems like someone who prepares everything one step ahead.
strings.dialogue.nodes.rin_intro.text: Mika Nakai. I mainly handle ward care. I'll verify inpatient preparation, handoff, and postoperative observations with you. When you need help from the ward, say exactly what you need. No need to talk around it.
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_boundary.text:
“Call it a Hoshimi specialty.”
She slides the last page into her folder, her smile carrying the calm of someone who knows exactly what she is saying.
“You can ask me for ordinary assistance or cross-department coverage. If something is beyond me, I'll say so myself. Being able to admit what you cannot do is also part of being a doctor.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_generalist.text: “Does that count as introducing your department?”
Soon after they leave the nurses' station, a figure rounds the corner and stops short. Sakaguchi checks his step just in time; their shoulders miss each other by inches. Several health-management forms slip from her arms.
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_intro.text:
“That was close. Are you hurt?”
She crouches to gather the papers, then looks up at the new badge on Sakaguchi's chest.
“Dr. Ryuji Sakaguchi? I'm Sayaka Nanjo. General practice, health management—and whenever another department suddenly needs a doctor, I may get dropped in there too.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_tease.text:
“And you've been staring at me because you're trying to remember a new colleague's face, right?”
Before Sakaguchi can answer, she has already stepped aside to clear the corridor.
“Let's record your answer as ‘yes’ for now. Don't be late on your first day, Dr. Sakaguchi.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.station_close.text: For your first day, remembering the three of us is enough. There will be more staff on future shifts, but you have met everyone you will need in the clinic and ward today. Come on—I'll show you your examination room.
strings.dialogue.nodes.station_haru.text: This is the nurses' station. The morning team is small today, so the names should be easy to remember—Senior Nurse Nakai, and Asakura.
strings.dialogue.nodes.station_walk.text: Sakaguchi follows Ren Nanase. She walks half a step ahead at a slower pace, pointing out the medication room, the ward passage, and the doors leading to the surgical area. The ringing phones and tapping keyboards of the nurses' station grow clearer.
strings.dialogue.nodes.yui_impression.text: Nurse Asakura laughs before anyone else can. Her Hoshimi badge is brand new, but the notes in her pocket already sort the hospital's equipment models and handoff sequence into neat categories. Her energy briefly lightens the busy station.
strings.dialogue.nodes.yui_intro.text: I'm Miyuki Asakura, and I'm supporting the clinic today! I've worked in nursing for several years, but this is my first day at Hoshimi, so I'll confirm the hospital's procedures from the beginning. You can leave blood draws, test arrangements, and patient transport to me. Oh—if I ask too many questions, don't take it to mean I can't do the job.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.diagnosis_re: She falls silent for a long moment, then touches her lower belly.
“Since you are already opening me up...”
“Could you get rid of a little of the extra fat here while you are at it?”
She goes silent again for two seconds.
“...Never mind. Pretend I said nothing.”
“...You have to cut my breast?”
She looks down at herself.
“You are not going to slice straight through the middle like a watermelon, are you...?”
“...No, at this size it would be more like a peach.”

She covers her face.
“What am I even thinking right now...?”
She is silent for a long time.
“It is not a figure of speech.”
“You really are going to operate on me.”
She looks at the doctor as though only now has she understood what all the previous explanations meant.
Her face slowly turns red.
“So... you will see a place very deep inside me.”
She falls silent for a moment.
“Even my boyfriend could never see that far inside...”

The instant she says it, her whole body freezes.
“...Did I just say something really strange?”
She makes herself sit up straight.
“It is all right.”
“I am not afraid.”
She nods with great conviction.
Three seconds later, she asks, “...Do you really have to saw through my breastbone?”
strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.encounter.fu: "Wait a minute, why do you have to take off all your clothes for a basic physical examination? Even underwear is not allowed?" (They said it too naturally. The clinic is not a dressing room.)

"That's pretty much it. Just make it clear where you want to check. Don't tell me to take it all off with just one sentence." (The medical record will probably say that I am not cooperative. Let them do it.)

"Okay, you said this is a requirement for a complete physical examination. I will cooperate. If you have seen enough, check it out quickly." (Speak harder, but still freeze when you reach your hands behind your back. No one of them evaded.) She was still unconvinced, but she moved quickly. After taking off all her clothes, she stood at the position you designated and completed the basic physical examination.

"...Okay. Since you said you would come in order, I will cooperate." (You really have to leave nothing behind. No matter how gentle you say it, it is still embarrassing to stand naked in front of them.) She took off her clothes until nothing was left; the doctors and nurses continued to prepare records at the original pace, and you then completed the basic physical examination.

"Are you going to press me for refusing treatment? Okay, I'll take it off and stop talking." (That's too despicable. But they were already waiting, and in the end they could only put all the clothes in the tray.) She gritted her teeth and took off all her clothes, letting the nurse take them away, and completed the basic physical examination with anger.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.exclusive_cg: Dr. Sakaguchi accepts the scalpel from the scrub nurse and holds it above the marked incision. Anna Takahashi trembles at the sight of the blade. “D-doctor, are you really going to cut me open?”

"Doctor, Dr. Sakaguchi is finally here. Of course I'm not afraid...it's just that it's colder here than I thought."
The incision has been made. The patient's reaction becomes apparent and Dr. Sakaguchi needs to decide how to respond.
Assign a nurse who is not part of the surgical team; the nurse can complete the preparation, or Dr. Sakaguchi can perform it himself. Choose up to two items for additional care.
"Okay, I'm ready. Don't look like you're worried about me."
The key steps have been completed and the surgical field has been confirmed to be correct. The surgery can now be concluded and sutures can be entered.

Please select the technique used for this time demonstration. The current version will directly calculate the time taken and the successful result.

"Are you really going to go under the knife? Okay...I will try my best not to move, but Dr. Sakaguchi has to remind me first."
"Hey, wait a minute! Where's the anesthesia? Dr. Sakaguchi isn't going to start like this, is it?"
Dr. Sakaguchi serves as the chief surgeon and three colleagues are selected to cooperate with Dr. Sakaguchi.

"Have you decided to have surgery?...I'm not nervous, I just want to confirm again."
strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.preop.title: Anna Takahashi · Preparation before surgery
strings.patient_bundles.patient_emi.diagnosis_re: She suddenly pulls her abdomen in tight.
A few seconds later, she realizes that makes no sense.
“...Would this make it easier to operate?”
She slowly lets out her breath.
“What am I even trying to help with...?”
She stares down at her chest for a long moment.
“...Will both sides still be the same size afterward?”
Without thinking, she cups her breasts.
“Why have I never seriously compared them before?”
“Of course I only start worrying about this when I need surgery...”
“I am sorry.”
“I know you just explained everything very clearly.”
She pauses.
“But it feels as if none of it stayed in my head.”
“All that is left is: ‘I am going to have surgery.’”
She stares blankly for a moment.
“You will be able to see my ovaries too...”
“What do they actually look like again?”
“They do not really look like two grapes, do they...?”
She mutters under her breath, “Why am I thinking about this now?”
Without thinking, she raises both hands and makes a parting motion in front of her chest.
“It is not really like this, is it...?”
Looking at her own gesture only makes her face turn paler.
“Why did I have to demonstrate it to myself?”
strings.patient_bundles.patient_emi.encounter.fu: "All, all... You can't even keep your underwear? Is this also the case for basic physical examination..." (The nurse is still there. If I say no, will it look troublesome?)
"Thank you...I won't take it off yet." (The body finally relaxed a little, but they have already written "Unfinished" on the medical record.)

"Well... since it is a rule, I will cooperate." (The buttons had to be unbuttoned by themselves. They did not turn around, as if this was not worth avoiding in the first place.) She lowered her head and unbuttoned her clothes, handed even the last piece of underwear to the nurse, and completed the basic physical examination in silence.

“I understand... After removal, it will receive a complete examination, correct?”
