strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_asuka: “I'm really tied up today. I'm not just using the director's work as an excuse. Ask me again another time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_aoi.i: “Sorry, I'd like to keep some time for myself this Sunday. Would you invite me another time?”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_rei.i: “I've got plans this week. Don't look so disappointed. Give me a little more notice next time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_emiko: “I'm busy today. If I wanted to go, I'd say yes. Another time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_artor: “I'm sorry, there are things I must finish today. If we can arrange it in advance next time, I'll give it serious consideration.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_shior: “I'm sorry, I already have plans this weekend. Thank you for asking. Perhaps another time.”
“No, no, there's still a problem I haven't figured out today! ...Ask me again next time. I promise I'll try not to bring my notes.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_sayak: “I really do have another commitment today. Don't be upset. I'll still be happy if you ask me again next time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_minat: “Oh, did I already agree to something this Sunday? Let me check... Sorry, I don't think I can this time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_har: “I'm sorry, this isn't a good time. It's not your fault... Could you ask me again another time?”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_rin: “I have some personal plans on Sunday. I'm sorry, but thank you for thinking of me.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_yui: “Unfortunately, I'm busy this weekend. Pick a better time to ask me next time, Dr. Sakaguchi.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_ang: “Thank you, Dr. Sakaguchi. But I'm not planning to go on private Sunday dates at the moment. I'll see you at work.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_hir: “Thank you, but I'd like to get some proper rest this week. Please ask me again another time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_moe: “I-I'm sorry! I already have something on this Sunday... Next time, I'll plan ahead earlier next time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_sat: “I-I'm sorry... I'm not ready this time. It's not that I dislike you. Really.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_pharmacis: “This Sunday I'm giving myself a complete day off. I can't even be bothered to plan anything. Another time, okay?”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_sakur: “I'll pass on a private Sunday date. Please keep professional questions for working hours.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_ish: “Sunday isn't an extension of the nursing department meeting. I'll pass on a private date.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_visiting_: “Not today. I haven't finished my analysis. I'll leave Sunday dates off the schedule for now.”
“Thank you. But I'm not arranging private dates on my days off for now. I'll see you at work instead.”
strings.ui.sunday.other_known_note: These acquaintances are not currently eligible for a regular date. Contacting them will not use your Sunday.
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_asuka: “Sure. A Sunday without approval forms is a rare treat. Where would you like to take me?”
“Today I finally got to be just Asuka, instead of the director. Spending an afternoon like this feels wonderful.”
“Wow, that enormous aquarium window was beautiful! I thought I'd only look for a little while, but I couldn't bear to skip a single exhibit.”
“A cherry blossom landed on my shoulder... Don't brush it off just yet. Let me stand here a little longer, like any ordinary girl.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_aoi.d: “Of course. It would be nice to spend some time away from the hospital. I'd be happy to join you.”
“I felt so at ease today. It's lovely to talk at our own pace, without having to rush to a conclusion.”
“Our coffee is nearly cold. Have we really been talking that long? Let's find another place like this next time, shall we?”
“I really liked that painting. Not because it's famous, but because the longer I looked, the calmer I felt.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_rei.d: “Sure! I've been wanting to get out and do something. Got any good ideas?”
“Haha, that was fun today. If you find anything else interesting, remember to invite me along.”
“Did you really guess how that movie would end? Come on, sit down and tell me everything. I've got plenty to say!”
“That fall of yours was spectacular! ...All right, I've had my laugh. I'll take it slow with you on the next run.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_emiko: “Fine. Send me the time and place. And don't be late.”
“You haven't wasted my time today. That's high praise, coming from me.”
“This is a good restaurant. The timing of each course, the cooking, all just right... Your taste in venues is quite acceptable.”
“That improvisation was beautiful. For once, there was a stretch of time when I wasn't thinking about my next operation at all.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_artor: “I'll keep that afternoon free. Since this is a personal invitation, let's leave work schedules aside for now.”
“You've arranged everything very thoughtfully. Thank you for giving me such a rare, relaxing day.”
“This meal suits my tastes perfectly. Taking the time to truly enjoy a dish is a luxury in itself, it seems.”
“A race to the bottom? I accept. But we'll check the slope and safety rules first. After that, don't expect me to go easy on you.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_shior: “Thank you for inviting me. Provided nothing unexpected comes up that day, I'll look forward to going out with you.”
“I had a lovely time today. You didn't try to arrange anything extravagant, and that actually helped me relax.”
“The flowers in the greenhouse are blooming so beautifully. We don't have to hurry to do anything here. Just looking quietly for a while lifts my spirits.”
“The cherry blossoms in this garden are beautiful. Walking with you like this, without worrying what anyone around us might think... I really like it.”
“A date? Of course! Just a moment, let me put this page of case notes away!”
“Today was so much fun! There's so much outside the hospital worth studying—oh, I mean, worth enjoying!”
“Did you see that fish? The way it reproduces is fascinating! ...Huh? You brought me to look at fish, not to give a lecture?”
“The sea breeze feels wonderful! If only I could take this feeling back to the examination room. Just kidding. Today I just want to have a little more fun!”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_sayak: “Sure. You pick the place, and I'll judge how well you've chosen. How's that? Fair enough, right?”
“Going out with you never gets boring. So, do you want to ask me out again next Sunday?”
“This little Italian place is really nice. Good food, just the right atmosphere... And the person sitting across from me certainly knows how to pick a venue.”
“The sun is setting right over the sea. Don't rush off yet—with all this wind, borrowing your hand to hold isn't too much to ask, is it?”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_minat: “Sure! What time shall we meet? ...Wait a moment, I'll put it on my calendar myself.”
“Today was so much fun. I remember all those little things we talked about, though I'll still have to write down when we're meeting next.”
“You still don't like much sugar in your coffee, right? You mentioned it last time. I'm much better at remembering people's preferences than my schedule.”
“Wasn't that dog by the river just like the one you told me about back home? Oh dear, I remember things like that, but I nearly forgot to check the time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_har: “If we're just going for a relaxed stroll... I'd like to. Thank you for inviting me.”
“I had such a lovely day. Who knew that just chatting together about nothing in particular could make me feel so happy?”
“While we were browsing the shops, I almost forgot we have work tomorrow. It's lovely to take our time choosing things, just like ordinary people.”
“The smell of coffee here is so comforting. We talked about so many little things besides work today. I really like spending time like this.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_rin: “Of course. Just let me know the time, and I'll be there punctually.”
“I had a lovely time today. Being with you is always relaxing. We don't have to find something to talk about every minute.”
“This is such a lovely tune. It feels like ages since I could relax enough to listen quietly to a song from beginning to end.”
“It's so pleasant to walk slowly along the sea. Sometimes it's nice just to listen to the waves, without rushing to say anything, isn't it?”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_yui: “Sure. But don't think changing into casual clothes will suddenly turn me into an agreeable newcomer.”
“Hmph, today was more interesting than I expected. Not bad. You actually know how to plan an outing.”
“You browse shops more slowly than a newcomer checks instruments. Come on, keep up—there's still plenty to see on this street.”
“At last, I don't have to remind anyone they're standing in the sterile zone! The sea breeze, the sunshine, and that thoroughly off-duty look on your face... Today was good.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_hir: “Sure. On a rare day off, I'd like to leave everything unplanned and just take a walk.”
“It feels like I've been the one being looked after all day. Thank you. It's so nice to slow down like this.”
“These flowers are so well cared for. Today I don't have to do anything, just stand here and look... That's a rare feeling.”
“The autumn leaves at this old temple are beautiful. Walking slowly, listening to the fallen leaves beneath our feet, I don't feel like hurrying home at all.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_moe: “R-Really? Then I'll check how to get there in advance!”
“I was so nervous at first, but as we kept talking, I forgot to be nervous. Thank you for spending today with me.”
“Is that little fish looking at us? Oh, it's swimming over! This place is so interesting. I'd like to watch a little longer.”
“There are so many delicious things on this street! But I can't just keep staring at the shops... Dr. Sakaguchi, which way would you like to go first?”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_nurse_sat: “Going out... just the two of us? I-If it's somewhere quiet, I'd like to try.”
“Thank you, Mr. Sakaguchi. Today I didn't keep looking down the whole time... I'm happy we could take our time talking like this.”
“I've read this book before. Oh, if you don't mind me speaking slowly, I'd like to tell you about the interesting parts...”
“It's so quiet in the greenhouse. We can walk side by side like this, without having to keep talking face to face... I feel very much at ease.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_pharmacis: “Sure! On a rare day off, of course we should find something comfortable and interesting to do.”
“That was pretty good. Going out with you is much easier than spending all day as a surgical assistant.”
“I only meant to buy one book, so how did I end up choosing three? It's all your fault for making browsing so much fun!”
“This exhibition is quite interesting. Every painting gives us something to talk about. It's a pleasant way to spend time, with no need to rush anywhere.”
strings.collections.character_events.sayaka_lv2_: Sayaka knocks on the door with a chart in her arms. Once the work is done, she doesn't leave right away.
Two light knocks sounded at the office door. Sakaguchi looked up to find Sayaka standing there with a chart folder in her arms and a pen tucked into her white coat pocket.
“Depends on what you're holding. I take it you're not here to ask when I'm free to go out?”
“Work. Don't worry, I'm not here to bother you.”
Sayaka set the chart on the desk and gave a little laugh.
“The way you emphasize that only makes it sound more suspicious.”
“Then read the chart before you get suspicious. I've checked the medication history again. The records are consistent, and this value is fine too.”
She opened the records and pointed straight to the two places she had marked.
“We still need to confirm this afternoon's review. If nothing changes, we follow the original plan. If anything does, I'll come find you. No need to chase me all over the hospital.”
“You've already organized everything I was going to ask about.”
“Because I really am here to work. Here, just sign this.”
Sakaguchi checked the details and signed. Sayaka took the chart back and clipped the relevant documents into place again.
“Good, that's the business taken care of. I'll take this chart back with me.”
Sayaka didn't leave immediately. Holding the folder against her chest, she let out a soft breath and leaned against the desk.
“I've just been back and forth between the clinic and the ward several times. Can't I linger for two minutes? Let me catch my breath.”
“Sure. As long as you don't hand me your entire afternoon's work while you're at it.”
“In your dreams. My own patients are still waiting for me. Just two minutes. That's more like it.”
She glanced down at the documents in her arms, pulled out an extra sheet that hadn't been filed yet, and held it out to Sakaguchi.
“Oh, put this one in for me. My hands are full.”
“You certainly know how to put people to work.”
Sakaguchi put the sheet in the right place in the chart folder. Sayaka checked it and gathered everything up.
“The person helping me. If you don't like it, I'll say something else next time.”
She spoke with a perfectly straight face, but her eyes were full of laughter.
“You're acting pretty normal today, though. I thought you'd go all strictly professional when you saw me.”
“How should I act? Start discussing our next date in the hospital corridor?”
“Some men are smooth talkers on the weekend, then put their white coats back on Monday and pretend they don't know you. Of course the work has to get done. You don't have to act so stiff.”
“So bringing me the chart was also a chance to see whether I'd pretend not to know you?”
“Hey, I took care of the actual work first. As for the other part… you can work that out yourself.”
Sakaguchi glanced at her, his eyes lingering on her white coat without quite meaning to. Sayaka noticed immediately.
“Didn't get enough of a look on your first day? Or has one meal together suddenly made you bolder?”
“We didn't know each other on the first day. We know each other a little better now.”
“One meal together, and you're already brave enough to say that?”
“Not at all. Look all you like, but move your eyes up a little.”
She tapped her face with a fingertip, then laughed as Sakaguchi raised his eyes.
You look really sexy in that
“Only noticing now? You were so well-behaved when we first met.”
“I didn't dare say it before. I thought you'd assume I was just staring at your clothes.”
“Oh? You're getting braver rather quickly. That's fine. I don't mind a good compliment.”
She arched her brows, clearly not about to stop teasing him over a single compliment.
Sayaka had been smiling, but the word “really” caught her off guard for a moment.
“…What's gotten into you today? A moment ago you were a doctor carefully checking a chart. Now you're suddenly quite the charmer.”
She briefly looked away. When she looked back, her smile had grown.
“All right, I'll take that. But don't think one nice line gets you out of writing up charts. I won't let you skip a single one that needs your signature.”
This time Sayaka really did pause in surprise, apparently not expecting Sakaguchi to choose that outfit.
“…Scrubs? With the cap and the mask on, half my face covered, you can still tell?”
She stared at Sakaguchi for two seconds, then her eyes finally curved into a smile.
“Of course. At least you've got good taste.”
“By the way, did you wear a white coat like this when you worked in the girls' school infirmary?”
“Of course not. If I'd gone to work looking like this, the parents would have come looking for me before the students did.”
“You have a lot to say, don't you? I was a perfectly respectable school nurse. The work wasn't much easier than it is now.”
She shifted into a more comfortable position against the desk, as though remembering a few things that had left her unsure whether to laugh or sigh.
“All sorts came to the infirmary. Girls who'd twisted an ankle in PE, girls white as a sheet from period cramps who still insisted they were fine, and girls faking stomachaches to get out of math.”
“You took in the ones who were faking it too?”
“I could tell by the third visit. But sometimes I'd still let her lie down for a while before going back to class.”
“You knew she wasn't ill, and you still let her rest?”

“Sometimes it wasn't a stomachache. She just really didn't want to go back to class that day. If someone's come to the infirmary three times already, you should at least ask why she doesn't want to go back.”
“Sounds like you were busier than the classroom teachers.”
“We each had our own troubles. Anyway, once someone was in front of me, I'd look for what I could see and ask what I could find out.”
She said it naturally, without trying to look as though she was teaching anyone a lesson.
“Some were even harder to deal with. Girls coming in crying over a breakup, sobbing away. No fever, but their eyes were so red it was alarming.”
“What else was I supposed to do, throw her out? Taking temperatures isn't all I can do.”
She deliberately imitated a student's wounded tone.
“‘Miss, yesterday he said he loved me more than anyone. How come he's gone off with someone from the next class today?’”
Sakaguchi looked at her. Sayaka couldn't help laughing first.
“Of course I didn't actually say that. I was still a very respectable teacher back then, you know.”
Sayaka pointed at her white coat.
“Now I'm a very respectable doctor. After work is another matter.”
“So you consider these two minutes part of work?”
“Of course. You still have charts to read, and I'm not ready to let you escape yet.”
Her words sounded stern, but her face wore that familiar mischievous smile.
“From the way you talk about it, you really liked working in the infirmary. Why did you go back to finish studying medicine?”
“I did like it. Sometimes those students were more willing to tell the truth in the infirmary when something happened. After two years there, I was quite sorry to leave.”
She fell quiet for a moment, turning the folder in her hands.

“But there were a few times when I knew a nap through one class or a cup of hot water wasn't going to be enough. I did everything I could, but for proper examinations and treatment, I still had to send her elsewhere.”
“You didn't like just waiting for news?”

“I didn't like that feeling of ‘this is where it stops being my job.’ Contacting parents and calling an ambulance were part of my work, of course. But once she was taken away, all I could do was wait.”
“So I went back and finished the rest of my medical training. I wanted to do more myself, instead of always standing at the door waiting for someone else to tell me the result.”
“Now that there's more you can do yourself, feeling good about it?”

“Of course. The hospital is much busier than the infirmary, and I still have to call in a specialist for cases I'm unfamiliar with. But at least I know when to step in myself and when to call someone who knows more.”
She looked up and smiled. Her seriousness soon gave way to her usual relaxed expression.
“So the main reason you left the girls' school was to finish studying medicine?”
“Sounds like there was a secondary reason.”
“I know. Being a woman doesn't stop me from liking men. Almost everyone there was female, from students to teachers. Barely seeing any men all day made me want a change of scenery too.”
“So you thought coming back to a hospital as a doctor would let you meet more men?”
She pointed out of the office door.
“This hospital's full of women too. Female doctors, female nurses, female patients… Did I change jobs, or just buildings?”
Sayaka looked Sakaguchi up and down, then gave a deliberately slow nod.
“Hmm… not for now. There's one more here now, isn't there?”
Her shoulders shook with laughter. It took a moment before she held the folder steady again.
“You didn't really go back to study medicine just for the men, did you?”
“Of course not. Medicine is the real work.”
She paused for half a second and winked at Sakaguchi.
“You're quite greedy. One meal with me, and you already want a five-star review?”
Sayaka glanced at the office clock and picked up her folder properly. Her leisurely air faded, and she was a doctor ready to move on to the next task again.
“Do you talk like this to everyone in the hospital?”
“And what kind of person am I?”
“One date so far. Good-looking, reliable at work, and I enjoy talking to you. Worth keeping under observation.”
She raised the chart in her hand and lightly tapped the records on Sakaguchi's desk.
“This is a hospital. Flirting is one thing, but if you miss something here, I'll still tell you off. Don't think I'll let you slack off at work just because you're fairly good-looking.”
“A moment ago I was a high-quality addition.”
“If your work isn't up to standard, even high quality can get downgraded. All right, my two minutes are already up.”
She put the pen back in her pocket and headed for the door.
Sayaka's hand had just touched the doorknob when she turned back.
“By the way, I've remembered what you said about me looking good in scrubs. Don't get to the operating table and pretend you never said it.”
“I wasn't planning to take it back.”
She smiled and raised an eyebrow slightly.
“Nanjo, one more thing. You look good in scrubs too.”
She had been about to leave, but turned back at his words.
“…Scrubs? With the cap and the mask on, half my face covered, you can still tell?”
Sayaka looked at him for two seconds, her eyes curving into a smile.
“Of course. At least you've got good taste.”
“But next time we operate, remember to keep your eyes on the surgical field.”
“Sneak a look if you can spare the attention. If you make a mistake, don't expect me to comfort you.”
She smiled, waved, and left the office. The door closed behind her. Sakaguchi set aside the documents he had just signed and picked up the chart he had yet to finish reading.
strings.collections.character_events.sayaka_lv3_: In the corridor near the operating department, Sakaguchi is checking a preoperative handover record. Sayaka stands beside him, holding the documents she has already put in order. The nurse handling the handover approaches, bringing along the questions the patient has been asking over and over.

In the corridor near the operating department, Sakaguchi is checking a preoperative handover record. Sayaka stands beside him, holding the documents she has already put in order. The nurse handling the handover approaches, bringing along the questions the patient has been asking over and over.

In the corridor near the operating department, Sakaguchi is checking a preoperative handover record. Sayaka stands beside him, holding the documents she has already put in order. The nurse handling the handover approaches, bringing along the questions the patient has been asking over and over.

“Dr. Sakaguchi, the patient’s preoperative preparations have been handed over. She’s still worried about having her arms secured. She just asked again whether she can pull her hands back under the blanket once she’s on the table.”

“Dr. Sakaguchi, I’ve finished checking the preoperative handover record. The patient has repeatedly asked whether she can adjust her hands herself once she’s on the table. I’ve noted her questions at the end as well.”

“Dr. Sakaguchi, the preoperative handover is complete. The patient keeps asking whether being on the operating table means she won’t be able to pull her hands back under the blanket. I’ve written down her question.”
Sakaguchi turns to the end of the handover record and checks the explanations and preparation arrangements.

“She’s asking whether she’ll still be free to move. Under the plan we’ve already agreed on, of course she can’t move around when she needs to be secured. Prepare her as planned. Tell her which step involves securing her and why, before she’s lying on the table fighting the nurse for the blanket.”

“She also asked me very quietly whether we’d have to lift the blanket to disinfect her skin. I told her, of course we do. What are we supposed to disinfect without lifting it? The look on her face was even better than when she heard about the scalpel.”
“You certainly didn’t mince words. Did she understand in the end?”

“She did, but she kept asking whether the blanket could stay on until the very last minute. I said we’d leave it as long as we could, but every area that needs preparing will still be prepared. Don’t worry, it’s all in the handover.”
“Then carry on according to this record. If she asks again, answer honestly. Don’t skip any of the preparations just because she’s scared.”
Sakaguchi hands back the checked record. When Sayaka takes it, she doesn’t look straight at the papers. Instead, she lets her eyes linger on Sakaguchi. The nurse handling the handover notices.
“Dr. Nanjo… were you looking at Dr. Sakaguchi again just now? I’ve noticed several times already.”
“Mm-hm, I was. Weren’t you looking at me just now, too?”
“I was waiting for you to put the documents away! I didn’t expect you to admit it so quickly.”
“I looked, so I looked. What’s there to deny?”
“Dr. Nanjo, you’ve looked over at Dr. Sakaguchi several times already.”
“Oh? Are you checking that too, Hiroko?”
“I just happened to notice. I wasn’t planning to put it in the handover record.”
“Good. If that ends up in a medical record, you really will have to answer to me.”
“Dr. Nanjo, were you looking at Dr. Sakaguchi the whole time I was speaking?”
“Yes. There’s no rule saying my eyes can only look at medical records while I’m working, is there?”
“That’s not what I meant… You just seemed very intent on looking.”
“There you go, then. I always look very carefully.”
Sakaguchi puts away the documents in his hands and turns to Sayaka. Even after being caught out by a colleague to her face, she makes no attempt to pretend she didn’t hear.
“So you really were looking at me? I thought you were just listening to the handover.”

“I can do both. I was watching how you handle your work. The patient was scared and kept asking questions, but you didn’t just tell her to relax, and you didn’t throw the agreed preparations into disarray. I thought you were pretty reliable.”
“Don’t flatter yourself. And when something needs confirming, you actually check it, instead of putting on an act like you already know everything. I like working with a doctor like that.”
Sayaka raises her eyes with the sort of smile Sakaguchi has gradually come to know.
“Your face. I look at your face too. When the man I like is right beside me, it’d be strange not to look. Do you really need me to put that in the handover record as well?”
“When you put it that plainly, I really do feel like you’re evaluating me.”
“I’m not evaluating you. I just want to look. You evaluate someone to decide whether you want them. I made that decision a long time ago.”
“If you’ve already decided, why are you still looking?”

She says it as if it were the most natural thing in the world, then lowers her head to check that the chart folder is fastened. Something between them has shifted a little, but the work in their hands hasn’t stopped.
“Should I leave you two alone, then? It sounds like you still have things to talk about.”
“Then don’t use romance as an excuse to slack off. I’m working too, you know. These handover documents still need to go back.”
“But you were the one who—oh, never mind. I’m getting back to work!”
Ren hurries away with her documents in her arms. Sayaka smiles and carries on sorting the remaining papers.

Work finally reaches a stopping point. Sakaguchi waits near the staff exit for a while before Sayaka comes out of the staff area, changed into her own clothes. When she notices his gaze resting on her, she pauses for a moment.
“What? Didn’t get enough of looking in the corridor today? Or don’t you recognize me now that I’ve changed?”
“I recognize you. But earlier you were clutching a chart folder and hurrying people along. You look a little different now.”
“Work’s over. I can’t very well go out to dinner in my white coat. Besides, weren’t you rather enjoying looking just now?”
“What do you feel like eating today, then? I’ll find somewhere with you.”
Sayaka seems not to have expected Sakaguchi to take up the conversation so naturally. Then she smiles.
“Anything simple is fine. Somewhere without too long a wait. I don’t feel like waiting for someone else to call my name again today.”
“Let’s head out, then. There’s bound to be somewhere nearby where we can sit down.”
“Sure. That sounds like someone who actually intends to spend time with me after work, instead of just saying it.”
They walk out of the hospital side by side, leaving the corridor and the sounds of work farther and farther behind.

They sit down in a small restaurant near the hospital. There are no special plans, no sense of an elaborate date. When the steaming food arrives, Sayaka finally sets her bag beside her, looking as though she has truly let go of work a little.
“You picked a nice place. We don’t have to study the menu forever, and we can sit down and enjoy a proper bite to eat. Coming out with you saves me worrying about where to go.”
“You’ve had enough to worry about at the hospital. After work, you can let me make a decision once in a while.”
“Oh, that was rather smooth. Are you learning how to sweet-talk me, or have you always been this good at looking after people?”
“I just thought you’ve been busy all day. At least don’t turn dinner into more work.”
Sayaka picks up the soup that has just arrived, but the heat makes her stop as soon as she tries it. Seeing this, Sakaguchi gestures for her to set it down for a moment.
“Let it cool a little first. It just came out. It’s hot.”
“Ah, I was just reminding a patient at the hospital not to rush to move around, and now I can’t even wait for a spoonful of soup. Have you caught me red-handed, Dr. Sakaguchi?”
“I’m not scolding you. I just don’t want you to burn yourself.”
Sayaka sets her spoon down again. This time, she doesn’t rush to follow up with a bolder joke. She simply smiles, quite naturally.
“Mm, then I’ll listen to you. Having someone look after me like this feels pretty nice, too.”

They eat and chat about ordinary little things for a while. Hospital handovers, shifts, and patients are not problems they need to solve at this table. Sayaka makes the occasional joke, and Sakaguchi readily joins in. The mood is more relaxed than on their first official date.
“Honestly, I really like this. No special plans—just sitting down to a meal with you—and I don’t get bored.”
“Me too. If you don’t want to go straight home today, we could walk a little farther.”
“Sure. I don’t want to call it a night this early either. Of course I’m happy when you’re the one inviting me.”
Only then does she pick up her spoon, now that the soup is no longer too hot, with an easy smile.

After leaving the little restaurant, they walk slowly along the street. Sayaka doesn’t immediately look for the shortest way home. Instead, she matches Sakaguchi’s pace as they pass another intersection.

“Something just struck me as funny. At the hospital, calling you ‘Dr. Sakaguchi’ comes so naturally. But after work, when we’re eating and walking together, using it all the time feels like something’s missing.”
“You want to call me something else?”
“It’s not just what I call you. We both know how we feel, but if someone asks, I’d still have to say, ‘We’re just ordinary colleagues who eat together now and then.’ It sounds ridiculous even to me.”
“What would you like to say, then?”
Sayaka stops and turns to face Sakaguchi. Her expression doesn’t become anxious or sad, just a little more serious than before.
“I’ve had my answer for a long time. But this time, I want to hear you say yours. If you want a relationship, let’s do it properly. We don’t need to keep talking in circles.”
Sayaka visibly pauses for half a beat. She looks as though she had a joke ready, only for Sakaguchi’s answer to get there first.
“…You’re bold today. I thought you’d have to talk your way around it a couple of times, but you were even more direct than me.”
“No. I like it quite a lot. Now that you’ve put it that way, I can say yes with every right to mean it.”
“Who gave you permission? How come I never got an official notice?”
“Then I’m applying now. Sayaka Nanjo, be my girlfriend.”
Sayaka tries to keep up her dignified act, but in the end she is the first to laugh.
“Approved. Is that official enough? But next time you plan something, remember to let me know in advance.”
Even though their relationship is settled, neither of them moves on just yet. Sayaka glances at Sakaguchi, without taking back what she just said as a joke.
“All right. Now that we’ve made it clear, you don’t get to pretend you never gave that answer.”
“I wasn’t planning to take it back.”
They stand quietly beneath a streetlamp for a while. Sakaguchi doesn’t start walking right away, and Sayaka doesn’t hurry him. She looks up at him, her eyes still holding a smile.
“What? Now that you’ve officially called me your girlfriend, all you can do is stand there looking at me?”
“I was thinking there might be one thing I still haven’t done.”
“Only just remembered? You’re not usually this slow at work.”

Sakaguchi moves closer. Sayaka doesn’t pull away; instead, she lifts her face slightly. He lowers his head and kisses her, and she naturally returns the kiss. After they part, she doesn’t immediately follow it with a joke as she usually would.
Sayaka lets out a soft breath, briefly looks away, then can’t help smiling again.
“…You were certainly quick about that. I was just thinking of something to say, and suddenly I forgot my lines.”
“It’s rare to see you at a loss for words.”
“Don’t get too pleased with yourself. I thought it was nice, so I wasn’t in a hurry to tease you.”
As she speaks, she takes half a step closer to Sakaguchi. Unlike before, there is no longer any need to explain the distance between them.
“…Well then, boyfriend. Walk me home today.”
“Can’t I? I’m not asking you to work my shift. I just want you to walk with me a little longer.”

Sayaka walks beside Sakaguchi. As they cross the road, the backs of their hands brush together, and she doesn’t move away. Neither makes a point of mentioning the word ‘girlfriend’ again along the way, yet they are already acting on that answer quite naturally.
At the intersection where they are about to part, Sayaka stops and turns back.
“Mm-hm. But don’t keep staring at me at work tomorrow.”
“Weren’t you the one who kept looking at me first?”
“I’m allowed to look at you. You’re not allowed to look at me.”
She deliberately puts on a stern face, but can’t hold it for even two seconds before she laughs.
“Mine. I’m kidding—look all you want. Just don’t miss anything in the chart you’re holding.”
Sayaka waves to Sakaguchi, turns, and leaves. He watches her walk away. Only now does this day truly come to an end.
Sakaguchi hands back the checked record. When Sayaka takes it, she doesn’t look straight at the papers. Instead, she lets her eyes linger on Sakaguchi. The nurse handling the handover notices.
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_nurs: Chat with Anji Tonegawa

Anji Tonegawa opens a small notebook, her brow furrowing more and more. Sakaguchi asks whether she has found something, and she closes it. “No. I used so many abbreviations in my own notes that even I can’t understand them a little while later. Records need to be readable. I don’t get to make an exception for myself.”

Anji sits down with a drink and stares at the cup for quite a while. “I spent ages choosing what to drink and still picked the most ordinary option. Don’t laugh, Dr. Sakaguchi. I’m not this indecisive when I’m making professional judgments… The choices in the lounge are harder, somehow.”

She opens the book in front of her, then closes it, as though struggling with herself. “I decided to take a break, but my brain is still reviewing my work. This is terribly inefficient.” Sakaguchi says that rest doesn’t need to be assessed. Anji gives a little huff. “I know the theory. Putting it into practice still takes work.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_nur: Chat with Anji Tonegawa

Anji stands by the railing for a while, pointing to the intersecting paths below. “The routes look so complicated from a distance, but walking them isn’t necessarily confusing. Teamwork is like that too, isn’t it? Knowing the procedures isn’t enough. You have to know one another.” She laughs at herself. “Did I just turn the scenery into another exercise?”

Anji carefully smooths the hair at her temples. “Nobody’s grading my appearance up here, but I still can’t help tidying it. Habit, I suppose.” Noticing Sakaguchi’s faint smile, she adds, “You’re not allowed to put this in my performance review.”

Standing some distance from the railing, Anji looks down. “From here, everyone in the hospital looks like they know where they should be going. But when something happens, everyone has moments when they don’t know what to do, don’t they?” She turns back, her voice earnest. “That’s why I don’t want to be someone who can only recite the right answers.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_nurs: Chat with Hiroko Sugimura

Hiroko Sugimura moves the kettle back to a spot where it is harder to knock over, smiling at Sakaguchi. “The little mishaps most likely to happen in a lounge are often the things everyone assumes won’t go wrong.” She points to an empty seat beside the table. “But this isn’t ward-round time. Sit down and have something to drink first.”

Hiroko sits alone with her cup for a while. When Sakaguchi approaches, she smiles and gestures for him to sit, but speaks first. “For these few minutes, I’m not sorting out anybody else’s problems. If you just want to chat, you’re welcome. If you’ve brought a third handover record, it can wait.”

She hears quiet laughter from a corner of the lounge but doesn’t rush to ask for silence. “Everyone focuses on efficiency when they’re busy. Having to vet every sentence even in here would be exhausting.” Hiroko smiles at Sakaguchi. “As long as they don’t disturb anyone trying to rest, I think it’s lovely.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_nur: Chat with Hiroko Sugimura

Hiroko looks into the distance from beside the railing. “You can’t see every ward door from here, but you know there are people behind them who need care.” She turns back with a smile. “A bit of an occupational habit, I suppose. Sometimes it’s nice just to enjoy the view without immediately worrying about someone.”

Hiroko straightens her cuff, in no hurry to go back. “Sometimes younger nurses are so afraid of making mistakes that they try to shoulder every problem themselves. But the whole point of a handover is to make sure someone else can take things on.” She looks at Sakaguchi, her tone still gentle, but entirely firm.

Sakaguchi asks what brought her to the rooftop, and Hiroko smiles. “Because at the nurses’ station, someone is always calling for their senior. It’s quieter here. For a little while, I can just be an ordinary person.” After a moment, she adds, “Of course, if something really is urgent, I’ll go back.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Chat with Aqua Mizuki

Looking down at the outside of the hospital, Aqua Mizuki gestures enthusiastically. “Something that looks complicated from below becomes a clear layout when you get a little higher! The body is often like that too. Change your viewing angle—” She abruptly lowers her hands and laughs. “All right, all right. No anatomy lesson today.”

Aqua changes her stance several times before finally nodding in satisfaction. “Same place, slightly different posture, and it feels completely different. Patient positioning works like that too. Details matter.” Seeing Sakaguchi watching, she waves a hand. “I’m just finding a comfortable way to stand. I’m not planning to test anything on you!”

Looking over the city, Aqua suddenly grows thoughtful. “If you get a good idea while you’re resting, does that count as rest or work? I was all ready to switch off, but my brain started a meeting without me.” She sighs, then smiles. “Oh well. At least I don’t have to write the minutes this time!”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_vis: Maya Ibuki holds a few sheets of paper beneath her palm. When she notices Sakaguchi looking, she gives a slightly awkward smile. “They’re blank, not research records. I left all the important material indoors. Sometimes I just want a different place to organize my thoughts.”

She gazes at the hospital windows and speaks softly. “In research data, a change can look like just a few digits. But behind those windows are real people waiting for their results.” As though worried she has made the conversation too solemn, Maya adds earnestly, “That’s why explaining results has to be about more than the numbers.”

Sakaguchi points to a stretch of reflective glass on a distant building. Maya Ibuki studies it for a few seconds, her eyes lighting up before she speaks. “Change the angle just a little, and what you see changes too.” Then she smiles, a little embarrassed. “Even looking at scenery makes me think about observation conditions.”

Futaba Sakura gestures into the distance. “If the hospital were a map, the rooftop would be a panoramic view you unlock for free. Shame there are no quest markers. You can’t tell who’s slacking off.” She glances at Sakaguchi and grins. “Relax. I’m taking a break too.”

Futaba switches off her phone screen and looks up at the sky. “After staring at data every day, it’s refreshing to find a view without scales or tooltips.” She thinks for a moment, then adds, “But don’t go designing an ‘optimal cloud-watching route’ for me. I refuse to give my breaks a progress bar too.”

Looking at the rows of distant windows, Futaba suddenly grows serious. “Sometimes the hardest thing in research isn’t strange data. It’s everyone deciding too early that something is obvious.” When Sakaguchi puts on his meeting face, she laughs. “Hey, relax. I just thought those windows looked too much alike.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Chat with Sakura

Sakura stands by the wall, letting her mind wander for a while. When Sakaguchi asks if she is thinking about work, she answers calmly. “No. Sometimes I’m simply standing here. It doesn’t need an objective.” After a pause, she adds, “You could try it too. No charge.”

Faint, intermittent sounds drift up from the city. Sakura listens for a while, then says quietly, “Usually, when I hear an alert, I have to decide immediately whether to respond. Not here.” She looks at Sakaguchi. “It turns out that sounds you don’t have to act on can be quite pleasant.”

Sakaguchi says it is hard to tell from her expression whether she is happy. Sakura looks into the distance. “I’m in a good mood.” She waits for his reaction before adding, “I’m not obliged to raise my eyebrows three millimeters to prove it.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_nur: Chat with Satsuki Orikawa

When Satsuki Orikawa sees Sakaguchi, she instinctively adjusts her glasses. “Dr. Sakaguchi… It’s much quieter here than in the wards.” She tries to find a suitable topic, then simply looks into the distance with a small smile. “Sometimes it’s nice not to have to explain anything.”

Standing a little back from the railing, Satsuki thinks of the patients she helps transfer. “When patients are wheeled toward the operating area, often all they can see is the ceiling. They don’t know where they are.” Her voice steadies as she speaks about nursing. “So telling her what happens next is more helpful than just repeating, ‘Don’t be afraid.’”

Satsuki takes a small notebook from her pocket, then quickly closes it again. “I came up here for some air, but I’m still thinking about writing down a nursing question that just occurred to me.” She glances at Sakaguchi with an embarrassed smile. “I will take a proper break. At least once I finish this page… Oh. That doesn’t count as resting, does it?”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_nurs: Chat with Chizuru Ishigami

Chizuru Ishigami sits near the lounge door. Seeing Sakaguchi standing, she looks up. “Sit. This isn’t a handover meeting.” Just as he takes a seat, she adds, “Nor is it an interrogation room. You don’t need my permission for your second sentence.” Her tone is calm, yet it sounds like a very restrained joke.

People are chatting quietly in the room. Ishigami doesn’t stop them; she simply closes the documents in her hands. “A lounge should have the sound of people in it. As long as they don’t disturb those who want quiet, there’s no need for everyone to stay on edge.” She looks at Sakaguchi. “I don’t run the nursing department by making everyone shut up.”

Ishigami looks at a densely covered note and folds it away. “Doing everything yourself isn’t management. If someone can take over, you should hand the responsibility over clearly.” She pauses, her tone as understated as ever. “Otherwise, all this hospital needs is one very tired head nurse.”

That Look from the Other Night
After returning to work on Monday, Sayaka catches Sakaguchi in the corridor.
That Look from the Other Night
strings.ui.sayaka_lv4.precommit: You have a feeling tonight may bring something good...
strings.collections.case_templates.template_adre: Right aldosterone-producing adrenal cortical adenoma (unilateral primary aldosteronism)

A solitary, localized, noninvasive functional adrenal mass on the right. Endocrine testing supports unilateral autonomous aldosterone secretion, and pheochromocytoma has been ruled out. The case matches the design scope of an ordinary open unilateral adrenalectomy; it does not involve invasion of adjacent organs or combined major-vessel resection.
My blood pressure just won't come down. Recent tests found a small tumor on my right adrenal gland.
A well-circumscribed, localized nodule measuring approximately 2.2 cm is seen in the right adrenal gland, with no invasion of surrounding organs or major vessels.
Findings support the right adrenal gland as the primary source of abnormal hormone secretion.
strings.collections.case_templates.template_dist: Localized solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pancreatic tail

A localized mass in the pancreatic body and tail, centered in the distal pancreas. There is no major-vessel encasement or distant metastasis, and a separable plane remains around the splenic vessels and hilum. The case matches the ordinary spleen-preserving open distal pancreatectomy design; it is not an invasive pancreatic carcinoma or an advanced case requiring combined major-vessel resection.
A checkup found a lump in the tail of my pancreas. I only occasionally feel some bloating in my upper-left abdomen.
Contrast-enhanced pancreatic CT
A localized, well-defined solid-cystic mass is seen in the pancreatic tail, mainly involving the body and tail, with no major-vessel encasement or distant metastasis.
Pancreatic MRI

The lesion has a relatively intact capsule, with internal hemorrhagic or degenerative components. Imaging features support a solid pseudopapillary neoplasm; a separable plane remains around the splenic hilum and vessels.
Staging imaging
No evidence of metastases to the liver, peritoneum, or other distant sites.
Pancreatic tumor markers
No significant elevation.
strings.collections.case_templates.template_left: The lesion is centered in the mid-descending colon, and its proximal and distal extent and blood-supply requirements are consistent with left hemicolectomy. It is not confined to the sigmoid colon, and there is no local invasion requiring an advanced multivisceral resection. This ordinary case follows the standard left hemicolectomy pathway.
I've had a dull ache on my left side for the past few months. My bowel habits are getting less regular, and occasionally I've noticed blood.
Findings consistent with mild iron-deficiency anemia.
Contrast-enhanced chest, abdomen, and pelvis CT
Localized neoplastic thickening of the descending colon, with no evidence of distant metastasis or disease requiring an extended multivisceral resection.
A circumferential ulcerated mass is seen in the mid-descending colon. The lesion is clearly centered in the descending colon and does not represent disease confined to the sigmoid colon.
strings.collections.case_templates.template_low_: Mid-to-low rectal adenocarcinoma (sphincter-preserving low anterior resection feasible)

Mid-to-low rectal cancer without invasion of the sphincter complex or levator ani; a distal margin and low anastomosis are feasible. This template is specifically mapped to open low anterior resection. In this first version, it does not share a case template with abdominoperineal resection (APR); very low tumors or sphincter-involving disease requiring APR remain separate disease and case types.
Lately I keep feeling as if I still need to go, but not much comes out, and there's often blood.
The lesion is localized to the mid-to-low rectum, with no direct invasion of the sphincter complex or levator ani. A distal margin and sphincter-preserving reconstruction appear feasible.
A localized ulcerated mass is seen in the mid-to-low rectum, with its lower edge approximately 7 cm from the anal verge.

strings.collections.case_templates.template_part: Localized small right renal cell carcinoma (cT1a; suitable for partial nephrectomy)

A small, exophytic, localized enhancing mass at the lower pole of the right kidney, with no invasion of the renal sinus, renal vein, or adjacent structures. Renal function is acceptable. The case focuses on removing the tumor while preserving the remaining renal parenchyma, making it a standard ordinary open partial nephrectomy case; larger, centrally hilar, or venous-invasive tumors are outside this template.
A checkup found a small lump on my right kidney. I hardly feel anything at all.
The left kidney shows no significant structural or functional abnormality.

An approximately 2.8 cm enhancing exophytic cortical mass is seen at the lower pole of the right kidney. It is relatively well circumscribed, with no invasion of the renal sinus, renal vein, or adjacent organs.
Serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate are within an acceptable range.
No regional major-vessel invasion or distant metastasis.
strings.collections.case_templates.template_vagi: Severe uterine prolapse (suitable for vaginal hysterectomy)

Severe uterine prolapse with adequate descent, stable cervical exposure, a modest uterine size, and good uterine mobility. There is no history of pelvic surgery or other strong indication of fixed adhesions, and imaging shows no large fibroids or adnexal disease requiring abdominal surgery. The findings specifically support vaginal hysterectomy; the procedure is not selected merely because the diagnosis is “uterine prolapse.”
Doctor, when I stand for a long time, it feels like something is falling out down there. Walking and using the bathroom have become really uncomfortable.
No cervical abnormality requiring a change to the current surgical plan.
Uterine descent is adequate, the cervix can be exposed reliably, and uterine mobility is good. Vaginal access is sufficient for vaginal hysterectomy.
The uterus is near normal size, with no large fibroid or significant intracavitary mass. Neither adnexa shows a mass requiring concurrent abdominal surgery.
